name: Hong for Wisconsin
subject: It’s about damn time
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Francesca Hong
body:
But it’s still not enough
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260220-2538)
Peter,
Last night, Wisconsin took a small but meaningful step forward on healthcare. I voted alongside my colleagues in the Wisconsin Assembly to extend postpartum Medicaid from 60 days to a full year. We unanimously passed Gail's Law to cover breast cancer screenings. Governor Evers will sign both into law, and it’s a win for working people struggling to afford care.
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260220.iNiycY&amount=5&refcode=em20260220-2538&t=19&akid=2538%2E105371%2E--Raq-)**
These bills had overwhelming support for years. The Senate passed them 32-1. But one man — Assembly Speaker Robin Vos — blocked them from even getting a vote. Minority Leader Greta Neubauer had to announce that she's pregnant and that her mother has breast cancer to finally force the issue.
That should never have been necessary. It shouldn’t require a statement from people who already have privilege, like our legislators, to take action. We shouldn’t have to beg for basic health care while Republicans go drink cocktails with wealthy donors.
This is what's broken about politics in Wisconsin: Basic, common-sense improvements get stalled for years while insiders argue – and working families pay the price.
Wisconsin’s healthcare system isn’t built around patients — it’s built around profit.
* 50% of Wisconsinites delay or skip healthcare they need because of the cost.
* Wisconsin has the fifth-highest hospital prices in the country.
* 40% of Wisconsinites have major difficulty paying for the healthcare.
* And our small and rural providers are having trouble making ends meet.

That’s not normal. It’s not acceptable. And it’s not inevitable. I’m running for governor to fix it — with a plan rooted in a simple idea: you deserve safety and dignity.
**Here’s how we deliver fairer, cheaper healthcare in Wisconsin:**
1) Expand and improve BadgerCare
We’ll expand BadgerCare, build the strongest possible public option, and take care of the people who take care of you.
2) Hold insurers accountable
We’ll crack down on claim denials, mandate coverage for necessary care, and make it easier to fight back.
3) Reallocate funds to reduce costs
We’ll put an end to price gouging, break up monopolies that close local clinics, and make hospital systems that get huge tax breaks pay their fair share.
**[Wisconsin needs a leader who’s not afraid to take on insurance companies, healthcare corporations and special interests](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260220.iNiycY&refcode=em20260220-2538&t=20&akid=2538%2E105371%2E--Raq-)**
**[So I’m asking — can you chip in $10 or $25 today to help us build the statewide campaign it takes to win and make this plan real?](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260220.iNiycY&refcode=em20260220-2538&t=21&akid=2538%2E105371%2E--Raq-)**
In healthcare, we’re all in this together. It’s time we govern like it.
— Fran
**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_fh_footer?refcode=em20260220-2538&t=22&refcode2=2538_105371_--Raq-&akid=2538%2E105371%2E--Raq-)**

name: Deb Haaland
subject: Governing isn’t a sprint. It’s a marathon.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
Running strengthens my spirit

| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/134?t=1&akid=7653%2E400544%2EuVSASd)
---
Friend, here's a fun fact about me: _I love to run_.

It’s a way that I honor my ancestors and the landscapes that sustain us. It strengthens my spirit, and it’s one of the many things that have made me clear my mind. **But I wasn't always a runner — in fact, I didn't start running until I was 40 years old.
**
**_[Before I share my story with you, will you please chip in $5 or more now to help me reach my $15,000 goal and deliver for New Mexican working families?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/4677?refcode=jtk273-fr-nd&t=2&akid=7653%2E400544%2EuVSASd)_**
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/4677?refcode=jtk273-fr-nd&t=3&akid=7653%2E400544%2EuVSASd)
I started out slow — running one mile, then six, until I finally worked my way up to 26.2 miles (and more!). As my runs grew longer and more frequent, my physical and mental preparation became much more important. In the 20 years since I started running, I've completed many marathons across the country.

Most importantly, friend: _My absolute favorite runs have been right here in New Mexico._
There's nothing like running through the canyons and soft sands of our landscape — and oftentimes, running past the petroglyphs and ancestral homes make me reflect on the strength of Indigenous people. In New Mexico, endurance isn’t just something you build — it’s something you inherit.
I've learned what it means to push through hard moments and that the things worth fighting for are worth working hard for. When your legs are tired. When the wind is in your face. When quitting would be easier.
And that lesson matters — because governing isn’t a sprint. It’s a marathon. I’ll bring the same determination and commitment I do to running to the fights that matter most for New Mexicans:
* Building an economy where working families can actually get ahead — not just get by.
* Strengthening our public schools so every child, in every zip code, has a real shot at success.
* Protecting our water and land so the next generation can run these same trails.
* Safeguarding New Mexicans and their families from the fear and extremism we are witnessing today

The truth is, leadership isn’t about flashy starts. It’s about steady progress. It’s about showing up every day, putting in the work, and refusing to quit when things get tough.

I’m running for governor because New Mexico deserves someone who will go the distance — for our families, our communities, and our future.**I'm in this race to move us toward a future where everyone can thrive, friend — and I know I've got what it takes to win in November. But I can't do it without you.**
**_[Please, will you chip in $5 or whatever you can spare now to help me reach my $15,000 midnight fundraising goal and win in New Mexico?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5042?refcode=jtk273-fr-nd&t=4&akid=7653%2E400544%2EuVSASd)_**

Distinguished Members of Congress,
I appear before you today not as a partisan actor, but as a concerned citizen, a parent, and an advocate for public health. The recent executive order issued by President Trump on February 18, 2026 -- invoking the Defense Production Act to declare glyphosate-based herbicides and elemental phosphorus as "critical to national defense" -- represents one of the most dangerous overreaches of executive power in recent memory. I wholeheartedly support Representative Thomas Massie's courageous introduction of the "No Immunity for Glyphosate Act" and urge this body to reject the President's misguided directive.
Let me be clear: This is not about agricultural policy. This is about corporate immunity, human health, and the fundamental principle that no corporation should be shielded from accountability when their products cause cancer.
Glyphosate -- the active ingredient in Bayer-Monsanto's Roundup and the most widely used herbicide in the United States -- has been at the center of a storm of litigation for years. The scale is staggering: over 200,000 lawsuits have been filed against Roundup's manufacturers, with more than 125,000 cases already settled for billions of dollars. Multiple juries across this country have found that prolonged exposure to glyphosate causes Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. These are not fringe theories; they're legal verdicts delivered by American citizens who examined the evidence and concluded that this chemical is destroying lives.
The President's executive order does not merely boost glyphosate production -- it effectively grants immunity to the manufacturers from the very lawsuits that have held them accountable. By classifying glyphosate as "essential" to national security and invoking defense production authority, the administration seeks to wrap chemical companies in the protective cloak of the military-industrial complex. This immunity provision is a poison pill hidden within a supposedly patriotic initiative.
I am not alone in this concern. The President's own Health and Human Services Secretary, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., and the entire MAHA (Make America Healthy Again) movement have voiced fierce opposition to this directive. How can an administration simultaneously claim to champion health while forcing toxic chemicals onto American farms, into our soil, and onto our dinner plates? The cognitive dissonance is overwhelming. When RFK Jr.'s supporters -- the very coalition that helped elect this president -- are warning that this order betrays the "Make America Healthy Again" promise, we should listen.
Representative Massie, a principled conservative from Kentucky, has shown true leadership by crossing party lines to defend the American people. His "[No Immunity for Glyphosate Act](https://substack.com/redirect/8c246c2b-c2e7-4e73-b116-db432ffd4ab4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" would strip away the executive order's liability shields and restore the right of injured parties to seek justice in court. This is not a Republican or Democratic issue -- it's a human rights issue. Congresswoman Chellie Pingree has joined Massie as a co-lead on this legislation, demonstrating that concern for chemical safety transcends political divides.
The science on glyphosate has become increasingly alarming. The World Health Organization's International Agency for Research on Cancer classified glyphosate as "probably carcinogenic to humans" in 2015. Recent studies continue to show connections between glyphosate exposure and various cancers, endocrine disruption, and potential neurological damage. While industry-funded research claims safety, the independent scientific community and multiple federal juries have reached different conclusions.
Furthermore, the international community has soundly rejected the chemical that our President now deems essential to national security. Dozens of countries have banned or severely restricted glyphosate use. The European Union has debated renewal of its license amid fierce controversy. America's continued reliance on this chemical puts us out of step with global health trends and at odds with our own stated commitment to wellness.
The President's executive order claims that reducing glyphosate production would "gravely endanger national security" because elemental phosphorus is used in military technologies like radar and solar cells. This argument conflates two distinct issues. Yes, elemental phosphorus has defense applications. But importing it -- or developing alternative production methods -- does not require that we simultaneously drench American farmland with carcinogenic herbicides or shield chemical companies from accountability. This is a false choice designed to benefit corporations at the expense of public health.
If the administration truly cares about national security, it should invest in American research to develop safer alternatives, support regenerative agricultural practices that don't require industrial chemical dependence, and ensure that our food supply doesn't poison the very people it claims to protect. National security means nothing if our children are growing up with elevated cancer risks from contaminated food and water.
I urge every member of this Congress -- Democrat and Republican -- to support Representative Massie's legislation and to resist this executive overreach. The right to seek legal recourse when harmed by dangerous products is a cornerstone of American justice. We cannot allow the Defense Production Act to be weaponized against the American people to serve chemical industry profits.
Stand with Massie. Stand with the MAHA movement. Stand with the 200,000 families who have lost loved ones to glyphosate-related illness. Reject this executive order and pass the No Immunity for Glyphosate Act.
The health of our nation depends on it.
Thank you.

This immunity provision is a poison pill hidden within a supposedly patriotic initiative. I am not alone in this concern. The President's own Health and Human Services Secretary, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., and the entire MAHA (Make America Healthy Again) movement have voiced fierce opposition to this directive. How can an administration simultaneously claim to champion health while forcing toxic chemicals onto American farms, into our soil, and onto our dinner plates? The cognitive dissonance is overwhelming. When RFK Jr.'s supporters -- the very coalition that helped elect this president -- are warning that this order betrays the "Make America Healthy Again" promise, we should listen. Representative Massie, a principled conservative from Kentucky, has shown true leadership by crossing party lines to defend the American people. His "" would strip away the executive order's liability shields and restore the right of injured parties to seek justice in court. This is not a Republican or Democratic issue -- it's a human rights issue. Congresswoman Chellie Pingree has joined Massie as a co-lead on this legislation, demonstrating that concern for chemical safety transcends political divides. The science on glyphosate has become increasingly alarming. The World Health Organization's International Agency for Research on Cancer classified glyphosate as "probably carcinogenic to humans" in 2015. Recent studies continue to show connections between glyphosate exposure and various cancers, endocrine disruption, and potential neurological damage. While industry-funded research claims safety, the independent scientific community and multiple federal juries have reached different conclusions. Furthermore, the international community has soundly rejected the chemical that our President now deems essential to national security. Dozens of countries have banned or severely restricted glyphosate use. The European Union has debated renewal of its license amid fierce controversy. America's continued reliance on this chemical puts us out of step with global health trends and at odds with our own stated commitment to wellness. The President's executive order claims that reducing glyphosate production would "gravely endanger national security" because elemental phosphorus is used in military technologies like radar and solar cells. This argument conflates two distinct issues. Yes, elemental phosphorus has defense applications. But importing it -- or developing alternative production methods -- does not require that we simultaneously drench American farmland with carcinogenic herbicides or shield chemical companies from accountability. This is a false choice designed to benefit corporations at the expense of public health. If the administration truly cares about national security, it should invest in American research to develop safer alternatives, support regenerative agricultural practices that don't require industrial chemical dependence, and ensure that our food supply doesn't poison the very people it claims to protect. National security means nothing if our children are growing up with elevated cancer risks from contaminated food and water. I urge every member of this Congress -- Democrat and Republican -- to support Representative Massie's legislation and to resist this executive overreach. The right to seek legal recourse when harmed by dangerous products is a cornerstone of American justice. We cannot allow the Defense Production Act to be weaponized against the American people to serve chemical industry profits. Stand with Massie. Stand with the MAHA movement. Stand with the 200,000 families who have lost loved ones to glyphosate-related illness. Reject this executive order and pass the No Immunity for Glyphosate Act. The health of our nation depends on it. Thank you. | | ---|---|--- | | ---|---|--- Thanks for reading! This post is public so feel free to share it. You're currently a free subscriber to . louder and stronger, until every community is safe.

At the Squad Victory Fund, we’re showing up for communities under attack,

clean_body: [] Peter, I just got off the stage with Bernie. We talked about the future of AI. Who controls it, who benefits from it, and who gets left behind. Bernie and I were clear: we cannot allow a handful of tech giants to dictate the future of work, wages, and democracy itself. But here’s the truth. Taking on Big Tech and Wall Street comes at a huge cost. I don’t take a dime of corporate PAC or lobbyist money. That means when I stand up to oligarchs trying to shape AI in their favor, I depend on small-dollar grassroots support from people like you. If you believe the future of AI should serve working families – not just shareholders – can you chip in $5 or $10 today? [] DONATE $5 [] DONATE $10 [] DONATE MORE [] If you’re with me, chip in whatever you can today. Thank you for standing with us. In solidarity, Ro Wait! One more thing– Ro doesn't accept a cent from lobbyists or PACs, meaning our work is completely funded by grassroots supporters like you. By donating just $3 today, you’re helping us create a country that works for everyone, not just those at the top. That means a renewed investment in American manufacturing, Medicare for All, student debt relief, and a green future. If you want to support our people-powered campaign as we continue to fight for progress in Washington, please consider making a donation of $3 or more today. Thank you! body:
| [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/103726?t=6&akid=23069%2E878179%2EJoUfoh) [I’m Chris Deluzio. I’m an Iraq War veteran, voting rights lawyer, dad of four, and I’m running for reelection in Pennsylvania’s 17th District.](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/103726?t=7&akid=23069%2E878179%2EJoUfoh) | [Donate →](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/103726?t=8&akid=23069%2E878179%2EJoUfoh)
---
Growing up right here in Western Pennsylvania, I learned the values we all know: hard work, service, and love of country. And after the 9/11 attacks during my senior year of high school, those values are what led me to the Naval Academy.

I still remember walking into Memorial Hall as a Midshipman, where we honor all alumni who have died in service to our country. Right in the middle of that hall is a flag that says the words: “Don’t give up the ship.”

It was a powerful rallying cry then, and it still is today. Some may feel like the country is on our heels. A sense of despair and maybe even hopelessness.

I think this is the exact moment we stand our ground and say: **Don't give up the ship.**

That’s why I’m running for reelection. Because patriotism demands courage in this moment. The courage to fight for our freedom, courage to fight the corruption and abuses of the Trump Administration, and courage to fight to restore the American Dream.
[Western PA: You sent a fighter to Washington, and I’m far from done fighting. Will you split a donation today between the Voter Protection Project and me to help us continue standing up to Trump and fighting for the American Dream?](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/103726?t=9&akid=23069%2E878179%2EJoUfoh)
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Chris Deluzio and VPP will go through immediately:

Since taking office again, Donald Trump has made it clear: he doesn’t share the same values that we do in Western PA.

Trump and his administration have pitted Americans against Americans. We’ve seen them call their neighbors terrorists, they took a sledgehammer to the VA, and they even weaponized the Justice Department in an attempt to intimidate me and some of my colleagues for stating the law and the basic truth of the oath we took to the Constitution.

And my Republican colleagues in Congress? They cower in fear of the President, falling in line with his pathetic agenda while he undermines our democracy and tramples on our Constitution at every turn.

**Friend, when my kids ask me what I did in the face of Donald Trump’s attacks, I want them to know that their dad fought back.**

Donald Trump is hoping that he’ll scare you away from speaking your mind, from standing up, from patriotically dissenting, from making your voice heard.

I know I won’t be intimidated. I’m not going to give these people an inch.
[I’m the LAST Democrat standing in a battleground district in Pennsylvania, which makes PA-17 a top target for Republicans. If we’re going to bring home another win for Democrats and Western Pennsylvanians this year, the work in this campaign has to start right here and right now. Will you split $5, $25, or more between the Voter Protection Project and me to help start off strong?](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/103726?t=15&akid=23069%2E878179%2EJoUfoh)

subject: The Drumbeat Toward War Is Back
body:
There is an alternative But only if we demand it.

| | | | | [|
---](https://roseforcongress.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=35bf91c695e8f4a5dc8a9dd42&id=1e8e2201cb&e=8c53948e4c)
| | | | | |
# The Drumbeat Toward War Is Back
---
| | Dear friend,
The same alarming headlines are in: renewed talk about military action against Iran.
**This is how it always starts.**
And we’ve heard it before: “Limited strikes.” Assurances that it will be quick, contained, and necessary. And then, years later, we’re still paying the price in lives lost, families shattered, veterans wounded, and trillions of dollars gone.
**War is not abstract.** It is children buried under rubble.It is our young men flown home in caskets or coming back with lifelong injuries.It is communities destroyed by bombs and environmental damage that can’t be undone.
And it is a massive transfer of public wealth - from our schools, hospitals, and infrastructure - to weapons manufacturers who profit from endless conflict.
We were told past wars would make us safer. They didn’t.We were told they were unavoidable. They weren’t.We were told there was no alternative.
**There** _**is**_**an alternative. But only if we demand it.**
**I’m running for Congress because I believe the American people are ready to say: no more endless war.**
---
| | In my next message, I’ll share what I believe we must build instead, and how peace can be an active, job-creating, life-saving policy choice.
Thank you for staying engaged, even when the moment feels heavy.
In solidarity,Rose Penelope YeeCandidate for Congress, CA-02People · Peace · Planet
P.S. Saying no to endless war isn’t radical. It’s responsible. And it starts with leaders who are willing to tell the truth.

Government officials cannot evade federal transparency laws by conducting government business on personal email accounts. Federal law requires the preservation and recovery of all agency records. Any destruction or unlawful removal of records must be investigated and remedied immediately. In that regard, we sent [a letter](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79791&L=37156&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL3VzYWRmLWZlZGVyYWwtcmVjb3Jkcy1hY3QtbGV0dGVyLTIwMjYvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=1f766317483ad1aefd0ddfdb8ac67acaf3c32111529cfd92c88f2a2f9a14c5b1) to Peter Marocco of the U.S. African Development Foundation (USADF) demanding compliance with the Federal Records Act following whistleblower allegations that senior agency officials used personal email accounts for official government business and that agency records may have been destroyed.Our letter details allegations that former U.S. African Development Foundation President Travis Adkins and former Chief Financial Officer Mathieu Zahui used non-government email accounts to conduct official foundation business, including communications related to government contracts, grants, and financial transactions. We have further learned that foundation records may have been destroyed.The letter asserts that the Adkins and Zahui emails sent through personal accounts are still government records that the agency is required to maintain and preserve. Concerning any unlawfully removed records, the letter states:As you may be aware, the Federal Records Act imposes a direct responsibility on you as an agency head to take steps to recover any records unlawfully removed from USADF. Specifically, upon learning of “any actual, impending, or threatened unlawful removal, defacing, alteration, corruption, deletion, erasure, or other destruction of records in the custody of the agency,” you must notify the Archivist of the United States.... Upon learning that records have been unlawfully removed from USADF, you then are required to initiate action through the Attorney General for the recovery of records.The allegations are particularly troubling in light of the [recent announcement](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79791&L=37160&F=H&&hash=6b306a9e6a7e901d3d8242b2b9775845dd640d0ecd4b1e076f79d964c3c519b0) that Zahui has agreed to plead guilty to allegedly accepting gratuities from a foundation contractor and making false statements to federal law enforcement.Should the agency fail to take these steps, the letter states that we are ready to file a lawsuit in federal district court seeking compliance:Please advise us no later than February 27, 2026, if you intend to take the action required under the law. If we do not hear from you by that date, we will assume that you do not intend to take any action. Veterans’ Facility Years after Judicial Watch Exposed Issue** Some good news out of Washington for homeless veterans in California: President Trump’s administration is going to restore a piece of property originally donated to help disabled vets. Our _Corruption Chronicles_ blog has the [details](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79791&L=37176&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvdmEtcmVjbGFpbXMtZmFjaWxpdHktdG8taGVscC12ZXRzLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=7f7cad71e91552896e9da23477c540457a3fc7f64bc1e9ecc4f06c151d338f05).Nearly a decade after an elderly Army veteran was federally prosecuted for displaying the American flag at the West Los Angeles Veterans Affairs (VA) to protest its failure to make full use of the vast property to benefit those who served, the facility is finally being reclaimed for its rightful purpose. Judicial Watch represented the veteran, Robert Rosebrock, back in 2017 and helped bring much-needed attention to the problem at the sprawling southern California parcel deeded to the federal government over a century ago for the specific purpose of caring for disabled military veterans. A California federal court eventually ruled that Rosebrock was [not guilty](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79791&L=37184&F=H&&hash=cde202b37d8ad6a4d4e67a501554e354d05e29084390c171d6adfa1751bda858) of violating federal law for displaying two four-by-six-inch American flags above the fence of the West L.A. VA but little changed to help veterans in need, especially the thousands living on the streets surrounding its lush grounds.Instead, the 338-acre West L.A. property, dedicated to the federal government in 1888 to serve disabled vets, has long been used for unrelated causes. Among them is a stadium for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) baseball team, an athletic complex for a nearby private high school, laundry facilities for a local hotel, storage and maintenance of production sets for 20th Century Fox Television, the Brentwood Theatre, soccer practice and match fields for a private girls’ soccer club, a dog park and a farmer’s market. For years Rosebrock and a group of fellow veterans assembled at the “Great Lawn Gate” that marks the entrance to the Los Angeles National Veterans Park to demand that the VA make full use of the property to benefit vets, particularly those who are homeless. The elderly vets were a thorn in the government’s side and federal authorities retaliated against them for exposing the fraudulent use of the grounds, including a [scam](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79791&L=37185&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvdmEtZmFjaWxpdHktdmV0LWdvdC1wcm9zZWN1dGVkLXBvc3RpbmctdS1zLWZsYWdzLWR1cGVkLW1pbGxpb25zLWJyaWJlZC1vZmZpY2lhbC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=416bcb04136e126857ad305aa1d6f10c18e0fc00505eca3aa7004b1157995b8b) involving a VA official who took bribes from a vendor that defrauded the agency out of millions. VA police harassed and intimidated Rosebrock and his troop—fondly known as Old Veterans Guard—at their weekly rallies and Rosebrock got criminally charged for posting a pair of four-by-six-inch American flags on the outside fence on Memorial Day in 2016. It is worth noting that Rosebrock’s absurd criminal charges were filed during the Obama administration, but the first Trump administration moved forward with the prosecution.Even after the elderly Army vet’s federal case got resolved, the VA continued to use the L.A. VA grounds for causes unrelated to veterans. The agency threw a few crumbs during the COVID-19 pandemic by offering a fraction of homeless vets [temporary housing](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79791&L=37186&F=H&&hash=c512e087ef22b57eec0df7396b46f087b81151fa71ceffd74419905c523e4ccf). Several small tents were erected in the parking lot of the VA healthcare system campus to accommodate a couple dozen vets who were sleeping on the sidewalk immediately adjacent to the grounds. It was a tiny gesture that barely put a dent in the crisis and Rosebrock called it a Band-Aid considering at the time there were around 4,000 homeless veterans in the city of L.A. Judicial Watch published somber photos of decaying tarps, tents, umbrellas and an assortment of ragged items, including large piles of belongings in white plastic trash bags, suitcases, lawn chairs, bicycles and wheelchairs, covering the swale adjacent to the VA fence on Veterans Parkway. The area surrounding the VA fence perimeter depicted impoverished shanty towns in the middle of some of the city’s most upscale communities. While droves of veterans suffered right outside the VA, its resources sadly benefited others.To right the wrong, President Trump issued an [executive order](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79791&L=37187&F=H&&hash=bc3090a123be0a15008ddadcff200ec8a052337ca1cb74132bc349c71f127501) in May to provide veterans with better care by, among other things, establishing a National Center for Warrior Independence at the West L.A. VA to supply care, benefits and services. “Previous administrations have failed veterans by allowing the West Los Angeles Veterans Affairs Medical Center—hundreds of acres in Los Angeles given to the Federal Government more than a century ago to help veterans—to fall apart,” the president’s order states, adding that parts of the property are leased to a private school, private companies, and the UCLA baseball team—sometimes at rock-bottom prices. “Los Angeles has approximately 3,000 homeless veterans—more than any other city in the country and accounting for about 10% of all homeless veterans in America,” according to the executive order. “Many of these heroes live in squalor in Los Angeles’s infamous skid row.” Finally, this month the VA [announced](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79791&L=37188&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly9uZXdzLnZhLmdvdi9wcmVzcy1yb29tL3ZhLXRlcm1pbmF0ZXMtaWxsZWdhbC1hbmQtd2FzdGVmdWwtd2VzdC1sb3MtYW5nZWxlcy12YW1jLWxlYXNlcy1hbmQtbGljZW5zZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=e993eb2c8f9234ab82033145dd9a14701c2c3f21c5889accb3c560a334009f32) that it is terminating “illegal and wasteful West Los Angeles” leases and licenses to clear the path for the construction of a center that will provide housing and support for up to 6,000 homeless veterans by 2028. The terminations will enable the VA to reclaim the property for its rightful purpose, the announcement confirms.Until next week,

In that regard, we sent to Peter Marocco of the U.S. African Development Foundation (USADF) demanding compliance with the Federal Records Act following whistleblower allegations that senior agency officials used personal email accounts for official government business and that agency records may have been destroyed.Our letter details allegations that former U.S. African Development Foundation President Travis Adkins and former Chief Financial Officer Mathieu Zahui used non-government email accounts to conduct official foundation business, including communications related to government contracts, grants, and financial transactions. We have further learned that foundation records may have been destroyed.The letter asserts that the Adkins and Zahui emails sent through personal accounts are still government records that the agency is required to maintain and preserve. Concerning any unlawfully removed records, the letter states:As you may be aware, the Federal Records Act imposes a direct responsibility on you as an agency head to take steps to recover any records unlawfully removed from USADF. # **[Trump finally gets his answer on legality of tariffs in new SCOTUS decision](http://trk.libertyledger.)**
---
In a major blow to the Trump administration, the Supreme Court has ruled against Trump's use of tariffs, a major part of his economic strategy in his second term. On Friday morning, the Supreme Court published its decision in the case Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump. The Supreme Court split 6-3, with the majority ruling that President Trump does not have the authority to impose the tariffs under the IEEPA.The case, which was argued in November, challenged the legality of Trump's imposition of tariffs through the invocation of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.

name: State Senator Andrea Hunley
subject: District 46 Newsletter
body:
---

| |
### District 46,
**Monday kicks off the _final week_ of the 2026 Legislative Session. **

As bills face final votes, one piece of legislation I want to take a moment to address is HB 1423--the bill that would restructure public education within the Indianapolis Public Schools boundary.

The supposed intent of this legislation is to address a couple of issues that exist within our Indianapolis Public Schools: **guaranteeing transportation for every public school student and ensuring all public schools adhere to the same accountability standards. **

One of the major problems I have with this legislation is that it would take power from the duly elected Indianapolis Public Schools Board--a board that is made up completely of women of color--and transfer it to a new board completely appointed by the mayor.

I will be offering an amendment on this bill to ensure that this board remains 100% elected in an effort to ensure that our community's voice isn't diluted.

Though we are nearing the end of session, do not let up on advocating for our shared future!
**I offered some more insight on this legislation and a recent IndyStar opinion piece ([ Indy's Black community doesn't need a White institution to speak for it](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "Indy's Black community doesn't need a White institution to speak for it ")) in the video below ⬇️⬇️⬇️**
---
| [ ](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D)
---
* * *
---
| [ ](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D)
---
### The Indiana Senate Democrats offered a dozen opportunities to make utilities more affordable for Hoosiers--Republicans rejected _every one_.

We cannot say as a body that we are fighting for utility affordability and then pass up on common-sense opportunities to do so.

Empty words do nothing for the family deciding between groceries and utility bills, the chronically ill Hoosier who has to choose between health care and air conditioning or the seniors on fixed incomes who pay their bills without fail, but they still climb every month.

My colleagues and I offered amendments to eliminate reconnect fees for people who have fallen on hard times, ensure lobbying fees are not passed on to consumers and create flexible payment plans for Hoosiers who need them.

Over and over again, we were told that this bill was 'too important' for us to take the extra time to address one of the most critical issues impacting Hoosier families. The real-life struggles of people in every corner of our state matter and deserve to be at the front of our minds and our conversations.

**When we say we are fighting for affordability, we are going to back that up. **

We stand ready and willing to collaborate with our colleagues in the State Senate to deliver real, substantive relief for our constituents who so badly need it.
* * *
###
---
# **The Kids are Leading __Now__**
---
---
### **I was honored to stand with Indy students making their voices heard.**
It is so inspiring to see our students step up when the moment calls for it--time and time again.

They won't accept moving backwards, and we can't either.

I am proud to stand with them and so grateful for every chance to do so
* * *
---
# **Zeta Day on the Hill**
---
|
---
### Honored to stand with the phenomenal women of Zeta Phi Beta Sorority Incorporated as we continue our legacy of service, scholarship, sisterhood and finer womanhood.
Using our voices is one of the most powerful tools we have. Voting isn't just a right, it's our responsibility. When we show up at the polls, we shape our communities and our futures.

**Let's stay informed, engaged and committed to the power of our voices.**
---

* * *
---
# _A Full Heart and A Commitment to the Work_
---
| [ ](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D)
---
### I was grateful to be presented a resolution recognizing my time serving District 46 in our State Senate, as I will be stepping down from the position when my term expires in November.
As this session winds down, and in the days ahead, I continue to carry the voices of our community with me into every room at the Statehouse.

Your experiences, challenges and resilience shape every decision I make, and I remain deeply committed to fighting alongside you to build stronger, more stable and more equitable communities across Indiana.
---
* * *
---
# **Know __Your__ Rights**
---
|
---
**Are you a renter? Is someone you care about? Attend this workshop to learn about tenants' rights in Indianapolis. ** At this event, attendees will learn about their rights as a tenant under Indiana law, where the protections fall short, and how to connect with other tenants to increase access to adequate housing through a unified renter base.
### **[Click Here to Register](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "Click Here to Register")**
* * *
---
|
---
### Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program
The Energy Assistance Program's (EAP) application is now live until April 20, 2026. You can apply [online ](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "https://urldefense.com/v3/__https:/www.in.gov/ihcda/homeowners-and-renters/low-income-home-energy-assistance-program-liheap/__;!!FlTQaCg!i0IlNmwztWy24u3OfjflEyvBopYLxqtX54ZBOGpkRIGHfA-g0F4tvn2RkRjwIClxVywwPaZ8QxM8BqUkhHdM0-IFVw$"), by mail or in person. To apply in person or request a paper application form, applicants must contact their local service provider (LSP). For more information on which LSP serves an area, be sure to check the map available on Indiana's [LIHEAP site](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "https://urldefense.com/v3/__https:/www.in.gov/ihcda/homeowners-and-renters/low-income-home-energy-assistance-program-liheap/__;!!FlTQaCg!i0IlNmwztWy24u3OfjflEyvBopYLxqtX54ZBOGpkRIGHfA-g0F4tvn2RkRjwIClxVywwPaZ8QxM8BqUkhHdM0-IFVw$").

In addition to this program, Indiana's utilities have financial assistance programs available, as well as other tools that can help customers manage their bills. You can find _[AES's program here](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "https://urldefense.com/v3/__https://www.aesindiana.com/payment-assistance__;!!FlTQaCg!jwpfitqHKx4bP-5cnhYvoAX1m8Q0kv3P901-pv7dMHXQdpRgas_bRhhF66AOaSuHe8tMuc2p6moGi_XjArAanOEmX3Q$") [.](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?%3D "https://urldefense.com/v3/__https:/www.nipsco.com/bills-and-payments/financial-support__;!!FlTQaCg!i0IlNmwztWy24u3OfjflEyvBopYLxqtX54ZBOGpkRIGHfA-g0F4tvn2RkRjwIClxVywwPaZ8QxM8BqUkhHfV2_ol6Q$")_

As a reminder, the winter moratorium runs from December 1 through March 15 and prevents disconnection of residential energy utility service to any customer who is eligible for and has applied for the Energy Assistance Program. Moratorium protection applies once a household submits an application and allows the Local Service Provider time to determine eligibility.

Utility bills continue to rise, and what should be an essential service has become an overwhelming burden for many families. If you're eligible, please take advantage of the available resources so you don't have to choose between keeping food on the table and keeping the lights on.

This is a step in the right direction to securing our elections. Read more about the brief below.WisGOP is also making big moves to build momentum and reach new voters. Recently, we launched a TikTok account to connect with younger voters and spread our party's message. Make sure to go check it out [HERE](https://republicanpartyofwisconsin.cmail20.com/t/y-l-atrkdll-didthutlhu-y/).-Team WisGOP **WisGOP Files Amicus Brief in Support of U.S. DOJ** The Republican Party of Wisconsin (WisGOP) has filed an amicus curiae brief supporting the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) in its federal lawsuit against the Wisconsin Elections Commission (WEC) and Administrator Meagan Wolfe. Filed in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Wisconsin, the brief urges the court to permit the DOJ's ongoing investigation into the state's voter rolls and to order the WEC to provide requested voter registration data confidentially, including personally identifiable information.

Accurate, up-to-date voter rolls, limited to eligible U.S. citizens, are essential for trustworthy elections. WEC has failed to maintain clean rolls, including not actively identifying or removing non-citizens, despite a 2024 constitutional amendment overwhelmingly approved by Wisconsin voters that restricts voting to U.S. citizens only.

"Wisconsin voters have a right to elections they can trust," stated WisGOP Chairman Brian Schimming. "For years, the Wisconsin Elections Commission has refused to properly clean our voter rolls, even admitting it makes no effort to identify or remove non-citizens who may be illegally registered. That position directly contradicts the will of Wisconsin voters, who in 2024 overwhelmingly amended our state constitution to ensure that only U.S. citizens may vote in our elections. The DOJ is simply trying to do its job under longstanding federal civil rights and election laws. We stand with them."

The DOJ lawsuit, initiated in December 2025, seeks compliance with federal laws like the Help America Vote Act (HAVA), which requires states to maintain centralized, accurate voter registration lists. WEC has resisted providing unredacted data, citing state privacy laws and other concerns.

Our brief represents hundreds of thousands of qualified Wisconsin voters and emphasizes that lawful elections demand regular maintenance to remove outdated, ineligible, or unlawful entries.

A copy of the amicus brief is available [HERE](https://republicanpartyofwisconsin.cmail20.com/t/y-l-atrkdll-didthutlhu-j/). **Take Action!****We need Letter to the Editor Signers!**
Become a Letter to the Editor (LTE) signer and help get the Republican message out to every community across the state. LTE volunteers are critical to continuing to advance our Republican values. Our goal is to have groups in every county who submit LTEs regularly. These groups will have resources provided from our team, including talking points, draft LTEs, and submission instructions. If you have any questions, please reach out to our Communications Director, Anika Rickard, at [arickard@wisgop.org](mailto:arickard@wisgop.org). [BECOME A LTE SIGNER!](https://republicanpartyofwisconsin.cmail20.com/t/y-l-atrkdll-didthutlhu-t/) **Become a Poll Observer!**
Missed the poll worker deadline? Don't worry, there's still time to become a poll observer. Sign up below! [BECOME A POLL OBSERVER!](https://republicanpartyofwisconsin.cmail20.com/t/y-l-atrkdll-didthutlhu-i/) **Help us bring victories to Republican candidates!**
Campaigns take money, and we need YOUR help to fund campaigns at every level. While Democrats rely on out-of-state billionaires, Republicans are dedicated to the grassroots and the State of Wisconsin. Help us show Democrats that Republicans are the party Wisconsin voters trust by donating TODAY! [DONATE TODAY!](https://republicanpartyofwisconsin.cmail20.com/t/y-l-atrkdll-didthutlhu-d/)

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. ## Supreme Court Strikes Down Trump's Tariffs
The Supreme Court on Friday ruled 6-3 that most of President Trump's [sweeping tariffs are unconstitutional](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGS4yAQBNCvkTJUYoRBFxBcosyXXqjCMNhzhzQqQGb991ve_YSNu6q7Xv-9rldHifb7H7ehrZHXHVtJWCvmtbpMMZZS8-n_B277GTmj57zCCFqMIECuwVF6raoPNiICTj1aaYzUBiSY_mHBmQmk_iUvOIc4K-MmKZXTSt4m7WfVk323jQBSynFWejDq4oIKtxmdwcukOzVioMp5-Me01wfG9OIn5sHz1if7qPUo3fS7g6WDpbU2RP54K955B8vBiSr50sFSziPjhsLzmasI6KkQ7yLw7lIQNZ_bIb7R4uCGufTZhqNRSlS06dR43xylr936o7OeFj4DAAD__2XrgMQ), finding he lacked authority to impose them under a 1977 emergency powers law. Trump quickly responded by [imposing a new 10% global tariff](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOtCAUhZ9GOwz3iuAUFH9jN3-7pUG4jOwiTBDHzNtv3H2E7U5yknPyfR_3-W5CDOnx32ykq89zonOPVCuVuZoSvN_3Wg775fKZDp8L2Vxm5CgZR4YwOxPiexat054IqW9Jg1IgFQKqdtXc8AVGUl71o1is8QKk8tYNasFBjq4N-lrjiADARyE7JQbjhFtGMoqGXjaCkws1l-4zh1RX8vGdX1Q6m7c26rXW5970_xqcGpzO8-zeZs35ahucLpwGJ1NqsJGuWMuxPZlJKR_J0s4eMS8mMuDsl5fBDXocbwDdWrfYFu2eZ4gx7FI1gj82E-LPdf2Tr5fG7wAAAP__jDd_sg) under a different statute, Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974. However, that law caps tariffs at 15% and limits them to 150 days, far less than what Trump had in place. The ruling leaves open a massive question: refunds. As much as $175 billion has been collected under the struck-down tariffs, and trade attorneys warn [the refund process could take months to years](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAYhJ8Gd1jwQ8ApKK5xl2uvtAj8xNxisADHytuvkn2E7UYa6dPM9--23GxMMT_-2g1ND2XJeLaEvWNduq0xhNZ6PdyXL2c-QqnoSl2AgaIMKPDF25heixy8CYiAYkDDteZKAwc9rEYKcVXAmA_q4oS42ukuUcmAk-XaBTZE86YxAM45m6QatbxYL_19QqvxIhSRDH3spY7_S8x9xZBe5Yl1dGUbkll73xsRfwjMBObzPEeX7-5dEpjfaAIzg08mMLdjr7ghdeWonfZ6bDv9-Uk9uthiyTSmhA-baMVwZN_GtW9pqMbvZ0wpNqWJZI_NxvRZ0H-l7WngOwAA__8qxoHp). The Court's opinion was silent on how repayment should work. Trump called the decision ["deeply disappointing"](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDEPmzAQhX8NbEb2YXAyeOjClq4dkbHPiROD0fkIyr-vUnXq2vHpSU_v-37d5ptLOW33n25Fy7HMG541IzPSzI5SjLUyHf4VyrkdsRD6QjNIGIUEAWoOLuXPrNtgIyJg36JVxqjRgALTPizgNcphVFcMg5EyovODuioVwtJLRN8m-12TAEopedFjZ_Tggg7LBZ3BoR8bLTEkLtQ9S9r4gTF_yhup82Vts30w77XpfzQwNTCd59lti_9SfPsGpr3kxMnXBqZ67IQrCl8O4n-zqEzphVUwHetexV96sbpnIbHkcoqdsKaAGwvymwOtL2BasmE_U86pjqbR8r66lP9c4__y-bbwOwAA____0o4c) and accused the justices in the majority of being "swayed by foreign interests." Democrats and business groups hailed the ruling as a victory for consumers.
## Trump Orders Release of UFO Records
President Trump announced Thursday that he is directing the Pentagon and other federal agencies [to identify and release government records related to UFOs](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAQhZ8Gd1hm_ENSUGzjLttuaWEYktnFYME43rz9le8r3O5IRzpH3_fnsTwsRUrP33ZDwyEvCc8akRnLwrZQCLVyOdw_n890hFzQ5bJAB5PsQIJavKX4WYbGm4AI2DdolNZq0qBANy_j-ttdT74b9aB0sBh6e9frffToVhXANWSutQ5AKdXdhqnVw2j94NcbWo1jP4mhQ0-cS_s3U-IXhvjJbyyty1sTzYt5r6L_JWAWMJ_n2bq1XhRXL2C-ooCZy7Ht8ghZ2kiYpE1e4n8ulrEUrFzIRhkpoAwUscodE9tnTgLmphi_nxQj1UmLoXtuluL3O_9I2dvAVwAAAP__UhODYA), unidentified aerial phenomena, and extraterrestrial life.

The announcement, made via Truth Social, followed remarks by former President Obama on a podcast suggesting aliens are real. Trump accused Obama of disclosing classified information, saying he might "get him out of trouble by declassifying." The Pentagon's All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office stated in a 2024 report that [no government investigation has found evidence](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOtCAUBeCnwQ4DVwT_guJv7GbbLQ3KZWQXZQLXceftN84rbHeSk3wnOZ-36eZiivv9w21oKeRpx7MmJMIykSsxhFqpHMu3z-d-hFxwyWUCAZoL4CAn72J6TarxNiACdg1aaYzUBiSYZrXgtQYndNcjOP2vN7PwXQDw8zKYYVZNtJcmAKSUYlC6Nap3Xvl5QGew7zRTAn2kXNqvHHdaMaRXfmJpl7w1ya5Ej8q6_wxGBuN5nu2yz8tVMhgvmsEo4J0ZjFSO7cGPyl2KuFd-hMzxh4ojLAUrlegSDzFhbVfaUlOsf5wxpVi1YUrcNxfTe5j-9NbTwm8AAAD__5i8foM) of extraterrestrial life. It remains unclear what specific files will be released or what they may contain.
## Ranking: World's Biggest Crops
Sugar cane ranks as the world's most harvested crop, with nearly 2 billion metric tons produced in 2024, far surpassing every other crop grown on Earth, according to [a Food and Agriculture Organization ranking](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFurDAQRb8GOpA9NpgtXLxmu31tSuTY42USg5E9C9q_j8gvpL5X50jn4zE_HCXanv_dipZjnjc8a0JmLDO7QjHWyuXlv0M-t1fMBX0uMwgYOwEdyDk4Su9Zt8FGREDVopXGyNGABNMuVgHgTenhFlTEyUxBDl4pHIU3gA5MS_aiCQAppZj02Bs9uKDD54TO4KDGRgsMxLn0X5k2XjCmdz6w9D6vbbIL814b9a-BewP38zz7g-rLJe92Ypeo8nW8plxSqN2aK3eLKwdWxtD5kvfawL0tNuwnpUR1NI0Wz9VR-lXwn7ocFn4CAAD__25LeQQ). Corn, or maize, came in second at 1.22 billion tons, with the U.S. ranking as the No. 1 producer in the world. It's followed by rice and wheat at roughly 820 million and 798 million tons respectively. Rice alone serves as a dietary staple for more than half the global population. Notably, many top crops are used as much for animal feed and biofuels as for feeding people directly. Most U.S. corn, for instance, goes toward ethanol production and livestock. Production is concentrated regionally: Brazil dominates sugar cane and soybeans, while China, India, and Russia lead in wheat. [You can see the full list here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFurDAQRb8GOpA9NpgtXLxmu31tSuTY42USg5E9C9q_j8gvpL5X50jn4zE_HCXanv_dipZjnjc8a0JmLDO7QjHWyuXlv0M-t1fMBX0uMwgYOwEdyDk4Su9Zt8FGREDVopXGyNGABNMuVgHgTenhFlTEyUxBDl4pHIU3gA5MS_aiCQAppZj02Bs9uKDD54TO4KDGRgsMxLn0X5k2XjCmdz6w9D6vbbIL814b9a-BewP38zz7g-rLJe92Ypeo8nW8plxSqN2aK3eLKwdWxtD5kvfawL0tNuwnpUR1NI0Wz9VR-lXwn7ocFn4CAAD__25LeQQ).

## UT Board Issues “Controversial Topics” Policy
The University of Texas Board of Regents has unanimously approved a new policy for teaching “[controversial topics](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL9ugzAQh58GNpB9JBgGD13Y0rUj8p8jXOXYCB8hvH1FKvUFup5On77v93Ubb4YCxfuneaDm15TGiHsOyIzr6FLkNT1xzWQCp4VcXlIgd4wgoK0EVCBHbygc46X02grfyxK1VEq26gp9X87agW8bUAqaqUHru8lZIzor0QrT2q4tSZ8wASAlCNlc64sVU2eldde-Ud6p4iLQE6e15hkZXyZP4TitapceZdAz85KL5qOAoYBh3_d6Si9ltswUz5cChrOpgGGL9I7ho3pzqsybx8i5OksxcsVo3Izr7-Evvcqb_UbHuVy1X3YKgXJ7et0fhsJbg_833lPDTwAAAP__9h-JPQ)” in the classroom, asking professors to avoid controversies “not germane to the course.” When “unsettled issues” are addressed, the direction calls for a “[broad and balanced](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O4yAURp_G7ojg2g5xQbGNu2y7pYXhYl8tMQhu_t5-5Ek19dSf9Omc8-86Xy1F2te_9oaGXyHNOz5rRGYss0s7l_TAUslGTplczSmSe88g4SwkCFCztxTfc996s0g_qhaN0lqd9QDj2G5G-k5ZUL4PAQev0Wmt7cX1vu8VDBpbMseZBFAKpOqGU7_IcFnU4oax097pppfoiVM58YaML1tDfB9UJ5dubTQbc65N96eBqYHJLdXeK9N-rA1Mh04DU0zOxgamO4sl2eJFCqLgijtXYXM-LKv4yImQimC0bqN9FT8aiE8E4bFmYhT5XrfFuv9tMT4_KUaq54N3vVmK33j8u6gPA18BAAD__0e-kPw)” approach where various viewpoints are outlined and discussed. University faculty spoke against the new policy in a hearing prior to the vote, with critics noting that “controversial topics” and “broad and balanced” are not defined. The Board asserted that _“[Vagueness](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAQBp8GOiN7CRAKF3-TLn97JTL2EvZkMPJuQnj7E-muvmablT7NzNd9uDuKtD7-uwWtvKc0rLhzRBHMg0-r5PTCzOSipI08bymSPwbQ0CoNCswQHMVjuJTBjjr0pkRrus60XQN9X85Wt9q0EEbssfFTfQXfmaabdNC1Dk2vS7LnmAYwBrSpm-oy6uk6mtE3fd0F3xUXjYEk5UpmFHw7nuJxUlU-LWW0s8jGRf2vgFsBt33fqym9T4vzX8DtyedZ6eMhh_pMKD5YcFEZWTJ5UYLOz7Q-1HNd0SOzyxQP9SuB4uf4jV64zDZsO8VI3J58j8VR_ODI3yK-LPwEAAD__3l3i7E) can be our friend”_ in a charged political climate. The policy differs from Texas A&M’s recent rules, which directly names controversial topics to avoid in the classroom, including “race and gender ideology.”
## Texas: World's Largest Data Center Market?
A new report from real estate firm JLL suggests that Texas is poised to be the [world’s largest](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAUhJ8GOiP7OEBcuNiGLttuifxzCI6MjeyzIbz9FXmF285IM9_Mv8f8MCGG9PxrNtT0WfKc8KgRibDMLicq-Y2lBhMp78HVPcfgzhk4DIwDAzF7E-I531qvLfdKtKjFOIph7EGpdtXW2h7cYqVybpFcet7fB4WKm5HfJdo26CuMAwgBXMi-u1m-3K2wrldy9G5sbhx9oFw6WpHwY-oSz4uqc3lro16J9trIPw1MDUzHcXSvGC-vgQkT-18bmK5RJX-lV4ws5UIrMxuW4AzzhgxzmAgLK7jnQuxEUxgmz4BD3xbt9yPEGOpw0Tw3E74FLf3usreGnwAAAP__FoWCRw) data center market by 2030, overtaking Northern Virginia for the top spot. Texas has 6.5 gigawatts of data center capacity currently under construction, which accounts for a fifth of the capacity under construction in the U.S. The report points to business-friendly regulations, as well as the availability of land and natural resources, as drivers for Texas’ data center growth, while noting that over half of the data center construction is in “[frontier markets](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLtu6zAQRL9G6mhwVy-zYHEbd75tSoGPtbUALSrkwrby9YH8C2kHgzmD83Wdr44Tr_f_7kFW3rc8r_SqiUSozCGvUvKTSmWXJG8c6pYTh31GjaPSqBDm6Djtc99G63U00JKFaYJxGtCYdrF9DG4A0uCBItJoOm_0EEdjQCOcTcv2GNOIAKihG06917ezBx8G000xTE2vKbLkcpKFhN6u3tJ-vDqF_GiTXUS22nT_Grw0ePn-OeIGL5-mik6cCrQKlapQd1p5viuhsKiXEyqKEgUpHFj2tti4vTglruNBvT8cpw9E_qbmafE3AAD__5kLeT8)” with similar appeal. The report comes amid some Texas residents pushing back against data center expansion in the state, with San Marcos and El Paso recently shutting down projects or voicing concern over the [strain](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLuurDAMRb8mdBklhuFRpLgN3dz2lCgkZohkCEo8D_7-KPzC6Sx5eWt5_zymhw0U9ud_u6Hh7xKnHT-ZkBnT5OLOKb4x5WCJ4xFcPiIFd06goJUKJOjJ20Dn1FTezMoPukKju0633R2GoVpN752ua1ysx7ptmg4BrVZt3yivoIe2CqaEKQCtQen6fmtmtfSznt19qDvvOtEo9IFjuvGKjF-bFzqL1c3FrSKzMh9Z1P8EjALGfKDj9NooOkvll0IJGPlblvHFq7wyJJI8bI4CxkIJGIuGgFHBNZeTi8vIkqMktF56y1Y63BmTzOg4JvmkOFuiU1bJ-OMTiEJui_Nzs4EuRf5bsW8DvwEAAP__Az6OCA) on water resources and the state’s power grid.
## Austin Beer Gardens Make U.S. Must-Visit List
Austin serves up two of the nation’s [must-visit beer gardens](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOtCAUBeCnwU4DVwUpKP7Gbv52SwNycUgYMXB3HN9-477C9ifnOzlfj-VhY4r79t--0NAn5GXHsyYkwrKseaeS31hqtInyEdd65BTXawEOsuXQgli8jelahsYbx70WDRqhlJBqBK2bp_HaBemkV7IXyvWjQEA-DTpo6aUNUxPNXcYBhAAu-rEbHA-TE24dda_8qtjA0UfKpaMnEn5sDem6V3VrfjXJPImOyvp_DGYG83meHdlKcd_IuoR3iMEMXGvJJwazw0qtQyztZovHvbbflcHcFOOPM6YUq7zJ7WVj-hXob7-8DfwEAAD__yZid2I), according to foodie publication _Tasting Table_. | Peter, The first big election for Democrats this year is here.
On April 7, Wisconsin voters will decide the future of their State Supreme Court. And with less than two months to go, the race is already exploding.
Last year, Democrats flipped the Wisconsin Supreme Court and secured a 4 to 3 majority. Now, with another seat up for grabs, we have a chance to expand that majority to 5 to 2.
If we win this race, Democrats could lock down control of this critical swing state court until at least 2030.
That means protecting voting rights. Protecting reproductive freedom. Protecting democracy itself in one of the most important battleground states in the country.
And the race has officially begun.
Liberal Judge Chris Taylor just launched the first major ad campaign of the race, warning that extremist judges like her MAGA opponent Maria Lazar are coming for basic benefits like BadgerCare and even trying to enforce Wisconsin's 1849 abortion ban.
Within days, Lazar fired back with a six figure ad blitz of her own calling Taylor a radical and absurdly claiming she wants non-citizens to vote.
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001QlrmHWNVFV83QtwcqgIikRKKPdlqyeQW4gFB-uYOeJlU0p80VpOevn1zuv3J5UwNU9cbtxH6wCIRbnkSMv4AMSgWum5ydHLRk3ydtqlL_ZFm-OdfoYMif3WwmTJzwz80KaPUiu_5Xxfv4D8s_a9MvmsbHtvVp-aXy1Gz4L5l2jCQwHHLd3j0FfNwsg58RLOFVZj3QN-buRIIvwL3uLd5X9QV-DY_t9Qt442CROWc_hc=&c=LG2xRRPqktnGKK4Z_wydGJiEYlDRoJO_R9i3UQlguBXJMoKyeLmr1g==&ch=CYZyVpYLeGuKnWfcP34ZXjVHsBYywhFyzRqLMjmq-tuoNZEtSmyzVA==)
---
The first shots of this race have been fired. It's now a dead sprint to the finish.
Right now, Taylor has the edge in fundraising, outraising Lazar by 10-1. But we don't expect this edge to last long. MAGA billionaires and dark money groups will be jumping in the race any day now to prop up Lazar and attack Taylor.
That's why Defend Our Courts is jumping in to help Wisconsin Democrats defeat Lazar. But we need to move fast to be prepared for the inevitable onslaught of MAGA cash, disinformation, and smears.
Last year, we helped lead the successful defense of the Pennsylvania Supreme Court, locking in a Democratic majority there until 2029. Now, we are taking our winning formula national.
Wisconsin is our first major test of 2026.
If we are going to stop MAGA, we need to build the war chest now so we are ready to counter every attack the moment it comes.
With more than 100,000 grassroots supporters nationwide, we have the power to be the difference in this race. But we need you on our side in this fight:

Dark money groups are spending MILLIONS of dollars to handpick your representatives in Congress. Their ads don’t even mention the special interests they really represent. These groups are pushing for politicians in Congress who will go to work every day for THEIR interests — not for the interests of the voters who actually live in the districts they’re blanketing with ads. Voters have a choice that these special interests are trying to distort: We can either elect fighters who will unrig this broken system or pick more of the same failed status quo. name: Douglas Carswell
subject: Introducing Mississippi Momentum: A Blueprint for Lasting Prosperity
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/msmomentum?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
**Too many young people still leave Mississippi to chase opportunities elsewhere.** MCPP is on a mission to help change that - by creating the conditions for real, sustained growth so our children and grandchildren choose to stay, build lives, and thrive right here in our state.

**The good news? Mississippi is no longer a laggard, but leading.**
---
|
---
_Young Mississippi wants change_
| Thanks to free-market reforms, we're now one of the fastest-growing states in the nation. **Over the past five years, we've seen more economic growth than in the previous 15 combined.** In 2024, Mississippi ranked #2 nationally in real GDP growth. Historic tax cuts have put more money back in families' pockets, flexible labor laws and affordable energy have attracted over $40 billion in investments since 2020, and fiscal discipline has kept us on solid ground.

Building on this remarkable momentum, the Mississippi Center for Public Policy recently launched our latest paper at an event in Jackson:**_Mississippi Momentum: A Blueprint for Lasting Prosperity_.**
---
|
---
_MCPP launches new report at event in Jackson_
| This blueprint outlines targeted, practical reforms to accelerate our progress and secure long-term prosperity. Key proposals include:

1. **Universal school choice** through a phased-in Education Savings Account (ESA) program - starting with thousands of students and expanding to make every family empowered to choose the best education path for their child.
2. **Healthcare freedom** by partially repealing Certificate-of-Need (CON) laws and granting full practice authority to Advanced Practice Registered Nurses - reducing costs by up to 15% and improving access, especially in rural areas.
3. **Conservative spending** to limit government growth to inflation plus population increases, protecting our tax cuts and generating surpluses for future relief or priorities.
4. **Welfare-to-work requirements** for able-bodied adults on TANF and SNAP, promoting self-reliance and drawing on successful models from other states.
5. **Merit-based procurement reforms** to ensure transparent, competitive public contracts focused on price, quality, and expertise - ending favoritism and waste.

You can read the full paper by clicking on the image below:
---
| [ ](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=6f5d38032c&e=5703353baa)
---
| It is thanks to your support that MCPP is helping set the political agenda in our state. The ideas we've championed are now at the heart of debates at the Capitol. We haven't won every battle for these reforms yet - but with your continued partnership, we will.

I hope you find our latest paper inspiring and useful.

**As someone who moved 4,000 miles with my family to make our home in the Magnolia State, I am more certain than ever that Mississippi can lead the way for other states in America to follow.**
---
| [Forward this email to a friend!](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=2c83251f4f&e=5703353baa "Forward this email to a friend!")
---
| |
---
In gratitude,

Douglas Carswell
President & CEO

| Peter, I want to update you on ICE’s activities in Maryland.

Alongside Senators Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks, I formally pressed Washington County officials over ICE’s secretive plan to convert a warehouse near Hagerstown into a massive immigration detention facility capable of holding up to _**1,500 people.**_

This proposal has moved forward without transparency, without community input, and without answers to basic questions about public safety, infrastructure, health care access, or human rights. **That is unacceptable.**

Planning a detention facility behind closed doors is not governance. It is intimidation. Converting a warehouse never designed for residential confinement into a mass detention site risks repeating the same inhumane abuses we are seeing across the country and here in Maryland.

That is why I also introduced the _Keep ICE Out of Washington County, Maryland Act_ , legislation that would block federal funding for this facility and give communities and lawmakers a clear legal path to stop it.

I recently saw firsthand the conditions inside ICE’s Baltimore facility. I will not stay silent as the same conditions are extended into Western Maryland. Our communities deserve transparency. They deserve accountability. And they deserve leaders who will show up and fight back.

Peter, **I know it’s Saturday. I know folks are trying to rest, be with family, maybe carve out a little peace before another busy week begins.** But the truth is — the work of protecting our democracy, our neighbors, and working families doesn’t clock out on the weekends. And neither do I. Because this coming Tuesday, Donald Trump will stand before the country to deliver his State of the Union address. **You and I both know what we’re going to hear... a speech built on spin, deflection, and outright lies.** So before that speech even begins, I want us grounded in something real — our shared values, and our shared responsibility to fight back in this moment. [_**If you’re able, will you click here and chip in $5, $10, $25, or whatever you can today to help me keep organizing, speaking out, and holding this administration accountable?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125830678/603052219/-522603632?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MmYyYzY5Yy0yZDBmLWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2E1NzU5M2YiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=KONiyzyuxwM2q93X2b-VSwR5Dey868alCpdNF5GgjSM=) **[HOLD TRUMP ACCOUNTABLE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125830679/603052223/-522603632?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MmYyYzY5Yy0yZDBmLWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2E1NzU5M2YiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=KONiyzyuxwM2q93X2b-VSwR5Dey868alCpdNF5GgjSM=)** Here’s what I’ll be thinking about while I am away from Trump’s State of the Union on Tuesday night: I’ll be thinking about the families in Vermont and across this country whose paychecks aren’t keeping up with costs. I’ll be thinking about people rationing medication, choosing between childcare and rent, working multiple jobs and still falling behind. I’ll be thinking about educators, nurses, small business owners, and workers who keep showing up — exhausted, but committed to their communities. Because that’s the real state of our union. Not the billionaire tax breaks. Not the corporate profits. Not the self-congratulations we’ll hear from that podium. **And what makes me a “hell of a fighter,” as some folks like to say, isn’t that I enjoy the fight. It’s that I care deeply about the people caught in the middle of it.** I got into this work because I believe government should make life better — more affordable, more dignified, more just. **It means having the courage to say — out loud — that we cannot build that future while corporate power and extremist politics are driving the agenda in Washington.** Trump’s speech on Tuesday won’t be about policy. It will be about narrative. About convincing people to accept cruelty as normal... to accept corruption as inevitable... to accept less than they deserve. **I’m not willing to do that. And I know you’re not either.** That’s why moments like this matter so much. Because while he’ll have a national stage and a teleprompter filled with lines to satisfy his very own billionaires... **We have something more powerful: people.** Grassroots supporters. Organizers. Everyday fighters who refuse to sit on the sidelines. [_**So I’m asking today — because this movement doesn’t take weekends off, and neither do the forces we’re up against — will you chip in right now to help power what comes next? Because if we’re going to take back the House this year and put a real check on this administration, it starts with what we build right now.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125830681/603052227/-522603632?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MmYyYzY5Yy0yZDBmLWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2E1NzU5M2YiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=KONiyzyuxwM2q93X2b-VSwR5Dey868alCpdNF5GgjSM=) I want you to know something. When I walk onto the House floor... when I speak out in hearings... when I challenge harmful policies...I carry your stories with me. The parents worried about their kids’ futures. The workers fighting for fair wages. The neighbors looking out for each other when ICE is in their streets. That’s who I answer to — not corporate PACs, not billionaires, not party bosses. **So yes — it’s Saturday. But the stakes are too high for any of us to sit this moment out.** Let’s be ready for Tuesday. Ready to reject the lies. Ready to demand better. clean_body: Before Trump addresses the country Tuesday, we need to be ready. | = Peter, I know it’s Saturday. I know folks are trying to rest, be with family, maybe carve out a little peace before another busy week begins. But the truth is — the work of protecting our democracy, our neighbors, and working families doesn’t clock out on the weekends. And neither do I. Because this coming Tuesday, Donald Trump will stand before the country to deliver his State of the Union address. You and I both know what we’re going to hear... a speech built on spin, deflection, and outright lies. So before that speech even begins, I want us grounded in something real — our shared values, and our shared responsibility to fight back in this moment. = = Here’s what I’ll be thinking about while I am away from Trump’s State of the Union on Tuesday night: I’ll be thinking about the families in Vermont and across this country whose paychecks aren’t keeping up with costs. I’ll be thinking about people rationing medication, choosing between childcare and rent, working multiple jobs and still falling behind. I’ll be thinking about educators, nurses, small business owners, and workers who keep showing up — exhausted, but committed to their communities. Because that’s the real state of our union. Not the billionaire tax breaks. Not the corporate profits. Not the self-congratulations we’ll hear from that podium. And what makes me a “hell of a fighter,” as some folks like to say, isn’t that I enjoy the fight. It’s that I care deeply about the people caught in the middle of it. I got into this work because I believe government should make life better — more affordable, more dignified, more just. It means having the courage to say — out loud — that we cannot build that future while corporate power and extremist politics are driving the agenda in Washington. Trump’s speech on Tuesday won’t be about policy. It will be about narrative. About convincing people to accept cruelty as normal... to accept corruption as inevitable... to accept less than they deserve. I’m not willing to do that. And I know you’re not either. That’s why moments like this matter so much. Because while he’ll have a national stage and a teleprompter filled with lines to satisfy his very own billionaires... We have something more powerful: people. Grassroots supporters. Organizers. Everyday fighters who refuse to sit on the sidelines. = I want you to know something. When I walk onto the House floor... when I speak out in hearings... when I challenge harmful policies...I carry your stories with me. The parents worried about their kids’ futures. The workers fighting for fair wages. The neighbors looking out for each other when ICE is in their streets. That’s who I answer to — not corporate PACs, not billionaires, not party bosses. So yes — it’s Saturday. But the stakes are too high for any of us to sit this moment out. Let’s be ready for Tuesday. Ready to reject the lies. Ready to demand better. And ready to keep building a country that actually works for working people. It wasn't easy telling the world I grew up dirt poor, I was raised by my Mamaw while my mother struggled with addiction.
It wasn't exactly the prep school/trust fund/summer-in-the-Hamptons upbringing that is commonplace in DC.
But I felt God called me to tell my story. Warts and all. I felt led to speak out because I believe millions of Americans share stories like mine. Stories of jobs being outsourced to China, addiction ravaging communities and killing our neighbors, and heeding the call of duty after the Towers fell on 9/11.
As your Vice President, I now stand in the breach for the left-behind, forgotten men and women who built this country, but were abandoned by the political class in DC.
I'll do everything in my power to make sure that never happens again. I'll fight every day for good folks like you.
