| | I am proud to announce that I filed my paperwork at the Orange County Registrar of Voters yesterday to appear on the ballot for the US House of Representatives in California's 46th District. I am excited to present my plans for renewing America to voters in Anaheim, Fullerton, Orange, Placentia, Santa Ana, and Stanton.

We need to address the failure of our welfare system, riddled with waste and fraud, and to reduce our national debt. I have a plan to phase out our welfare and entitlement programs and return the money back to the people. The money we would generate by reducing the size of our government would be enough to provide $16,000 per year for every American 21 and over, and we could still save over $1 trillion per year over the long term compared to our existing system.
We cannot create equal opportunity without providing a quality education for everyone. I will advocate for charter schools and vouchers that would allow all parents, not just the wealthy, to be able to send their children to the school of their choice.

| | I find it deeply troubling that anyone would attempt to use allegations involving the abuse of young girls as a political weapon. These matters demand seriousness, care, and integrity, not anonymous attacks timed for political advantage. Republican delegates deserve better than misinformation built on the suffering of victims.
I have always been open and transparent about my work as a prosecutor. It is disappointing that anonymous individuals have chosen to circulate misleading claims rather than raise concerns directly or address them in a public, accountable forum.
As Republican delegates prepare for county and state conventions, you deserve facts, not distortions.
Several assertions in the anonymous email now circulating are demonstrably false.
Most notably, the [ESPN article](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001vqRi4_WkXqqU3ok6uKvwThh52WcZRs-wsIMNSBpJqhGenj76XwRkXCo49RwWrNTYjmDVNWeoDlay12n3PIKgnBp4wV05TL_n1qAbei-ynutJxE44VzypKi47FuAHMXxeZsoQRAylqLiqXm-CKdkrckm39tYN4JxJXbY1ENfc7Fsda0HU0l-3fBd3YacIgPmp--e-n-vxtu1rmBwmIjaAkgITkctOWYUHsNbMlhVIDlhBl8kt3y5ZUNWgRvz3_grHx94pUL0QLoIXLHzuNiLFQs_FWhXFUPApWPNQTBkMd3I=&c=udoH4zz7egnnilWWY-S412YF_XaNjKgeT53YqFk0ngmsBLyMTeckYg==&ch=KtiygVLCFtYX9N7Kjb5P6VBfnTk6PBWcDa269tftOC24tqDvp9s2kA==) cited does not mention me, nor does it quote me praising Attorney General Dana Nessel. That claim is simply untrue. Misrepresenting published reporting to create a narrative is not advocacy; it is misinformation.
I also want to be clear about my role in the Geddert matter. I do not speculate publicly about charging decisions made more than a decade ago without reviewing the complete file, and responsible prosecutors should not.
When allegations resurfaced in 2018, my office had the case for approximately three months. Some of the victims were also victims in the Larry Nassar case, and the Attorney General's Office had already built established relationships and trust with them. The attorneys involved at the Attorney General's Office were the same attorneys who handled the Nassar prosecution during Attorney General Bill Schuette's administration.
For those reasons, I made the decision to allow the Attorney General's Office to handle the case. This was done to protect victims, avoid unnecessary duplication, and ensure continuity by attorneys already familiar with the individuals involved.
It is also important to understand that county prosecutor offices do not conduct independent investigations. We evaluate cases based on evidence gathered by law enforcement. The Attorney General's Office, by contrast, has investigators in-house and broader resources, which further supported the decision to defer.
Once the Attorney General's Office assumed responsibility, all investigative and charging decisions were theirs. After charges were announced in 2021, John Geddert died by suicide before the case could be resolved in court. There was never a trial and never a legal determination of guilt or innocence.
Questions have also been raised about a 2013 complaint involving John Geddert. At that time, my office reviewed the police report and concluded there was sufficient evidence to support a charge related to inappropriate physical conduct. The matter was resolved through a lawful disposition that included counseling and a written apology to the gymnast. There were no additional complainants or corroborating evidence available at that time. Prosecutors must make decisions based on the evidence before them, not on information that emerges years later.
Cases involving historical abuse allegations demand experienced prosecutors who understand evidentiary standards, ethical obligations, and the limits of the law. Oversimplifying these cases or misrepresenting the public record does not help victims and reflects a lack of understanding of how prosecution actually works.
Finally, I believe Republican voters deserve open discussion and accountability. Anonymous attacks released on the eve of conventions, while refusing to raise these claims publicly or participate in debates, are not how serious candidates conduct themselves. I have been willing to address my record directly and will continue to do so.
I stand by my work, my judgment, and my commitment to the rule of law.
Sincerely,
Doug Lloyd Eaton County Prosecuting Attorney Candidate for Michigan Attorney General

clean_body: | | | ** Cruelty is their point. There is no low that Donald Trump and his budget director, Russ Vought, won’t stoop to when it comes to afflicting federal workers and people with disabilities. After being diagnosed with a brain tumor, federal worker Helen Shaw, a single mother of two, was told her agency’s disability plan was getting axed before her surgery. Vought had just moved to slash disability, dental, and life insurance plans for federal employees. Denying disability insurance to a mother facing a brain tumor is a level of senseless cruelty that we cannot ignore. From slashing healthcare and food assistance to systematically "traumatizing" the federal workforce by eliminating benefits and job security, Vought and Trump are working to dismantle the safety nets that millions of Americans with disabilities rely on for survival. # [I proudly stand with unions](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=188544930&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg4NTQ0OTMwLCJpYXQiOjE3NzE2OTY5MzUsImV4cCI6MTc3NDI4ODkzNSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.yx3UGtZ4i3bItfMrgr81B27qngKM6l_JrwreQUQmyEI)
### Workers know I have their backs
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Feb 21
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack..5hpE_lPw5Inqdnwh7HZVOZBK3Cbc0bDOMJp863y15Sw?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/i-proudly-stand-with-unions?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Hi team,
In the middle of all the chaos and everything going on in the world day after day, what grounds me and keeps me going every day is remembering _who_ I'm fighting for: **The working people of Michigan.**
These are the people who keep our economy moving -- who build, fix, teach, nurse, cook, deliver, and care. The folks who punch in every day, take pride in what they do, and keep our state strong.
Fighting for working Michiganders is why I got into public service in the first place. And it's why I'm running for Senate now.
**I 'm proud to be the ONLY candidate in this race to have earned the support of multiple Michigan labor unions in this campaign, including:**
> ✅ Michigan Machinists Council
> ✅ IronWorkers Local 25
> ✅ Bricklayers and Allied Craftworkers Local 2
> ✅ Teamsters Local 243
> ✅ Pipefitters, Steamfitters, Refrigeration & Air Conditioning Service Local 636
> ✅ UNITE Here Local 24
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fc5c45ef-82c8-4a8b-8428-fce70485e32a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
These endorsements mean the world to me, because they represent more than just a rubber stamp of approval.
**These are people who know what 's at stake here. **And they know that when I say I'm with them in this fight, I'm ready to back those words up with action.
I've joined Teamsters on the picket line. I've talked with Michigan nurses fighting for safer working conditions. I've met ironworkers raising families and trying to keep up with the cost of living and Trump's erratic tariffs. I've heard from retirees whose pensions no longer cover their rent -- people who worked their whole lives and still can't catch a break.
_I carry those conversations with me every day._
They remind me of my dad, who's in his 80s and still working. I think about the folks who have to keep working just to survive, and**I know we can do better by our workers.**
Because here's the truth: **[There is no strong middle class without strong unions.](https://substack.com/redirect/5a895161-b37c-4a98-a0b6-01582cb81401?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
That's not just a slogan. It's a fact. When union power declines, wages stagnate, benefits disappear, inequality rises, and communities suffer. But when we support unions, everyone benefits.
**And no state knows that better than Michigan.**
We helped build the American labor movement: from the Flint sit-down strike to the Battle of the Overpass. And we can lead again. But only if we stand together -- and fight back against the forces trying to silence workers.
Because right now, **Donald Trump and his MAGA guys are coming after organized labor.** They want to weaken worker protections, strip away bargaining rights, and give billionaires even more tax breaks -- and they're targeting this Senate seat to do it.
But I'm not backing down.
**I 'm in this race because I believe every Michigan worker deserves a voice** -- and a Senator who's willing to fight for them. Someone who understands our state, who has walked factory floors and talked with workers for hours in union halls, and who will never forget _who_ they're in Washington to serve.
That's the kind of Senator I'll be.
And if you're with me, if you believe in the power of workers, I hope you'll consider joining our grassroots team. We're working toward our biggest fundraising goal yet -- and every dollar helps us reach more voters and build the kind of people-powered campaign it takes to win a battleground race like this. **[Will you chip in now to keep Michigan blue?](https://substack.com/redirect/5a895161-b37c-4a98-a0b6-01582cb81401?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/5a895161-b37c-4a98-a0b6-01582cb81401?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thanks for reading this. And thank you for standing with Michigan workers.
With grit and gratitude,
Haley
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1aa7245c-61fa-4ad7-98ca-826bc432361f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

* * *

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?

clean_body: Workers know I have their backs | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more Workers know I have their backs | | | Feb 21 | | | | | | Hi team, In the middle of all the chaos and everything going on in the world day after day, what grounds me and keeps me going every day is remembering who I'm fighting for: The working people of Michigan. These are the people who keep our economy moving -- who build, fix, teach, nurse, cook, deliver, and care. The folks who punch in every day, take pride in what they do, and keep our state strong. Fighting for working Michiganders is why I got into public service in the first place. And it's why I'm running for Senate now. I 'm proud to be the ONLY candidate in this race to have earned the support of multiple Michigan labor unions in this campaign, including: ✅ Michigan Machinists Council ✅ IronWorkers Local 25 ✅ Bricklayers and Allied Craftworkers Local 2 ✅ Teamsters Local 243 ✅ Pipefitters, Steamfitters, Refrigeration & Air Conditioning Service Local 636 ✅ UNITE Here Local 24 | | ---|---|--- These endorsements mean the world to me, because they represent more than just a rubber stamp of approval. These are people who know what 's at stake here. And they know that when I say I'm with them in this fight, I'm ready to back those words up with action. I've joined Teamsters on the picket line. I've talked with Michigan nurses fighting for safer working conditions. I've met ironworkers raising families and trying to keep up with the cost of living and Trump's erratic tariffs. I've heard from retirees whose pensions no longer cover their rent -- people who worked their whole lives and still can't catch a break. I carry those conversations with me every day. They remind me of my dad, who's in his 80s and still working. I think about the folks who have to keep working just to survive, andI know we can do better by our workers. Because here's the truth: That's not just a slogan. It's a fact. When union power declines, wages stagnate, benefits disappear, inequality rises, and communities suffer. But when we support unions, everyone benefits. And no state knows that better than Michigan. We helped build the American labor movement: from the Flint sit-down strike to the Battle of the Overpass. And we can lead again. But only if we stand together -- and fight back against the forces trying to silence workers. Because right now, Donald Trump and his MAGA guys are coming after organized labor. They want to weaken worker protections, strip away bargaining rights, and give billionaires even more tax breaks -- and they're targeting this Senate seat to do it. But I'm not backing down. I 'm in this race because I believe every Michigan worker deserves a voice -- and a Senator who's willing to fight for them. Someone who understands our state, who has walked factory floors and talked with workers for hours in union halls, and who will never forget who they're in Washington to serve. That's the kind of Senator I'll be. And if you're with me, if you believe in the power of workers, I hope you'll consider joining our grassroots team. We're working toward our biggest fundraising goal yet -- and every dollar helps us reach more voters and build the kind of people-powered campaign it takes to win a battleground race like this. Thanks for reading this. And thank you for standing with Michigan workers. With grit and gratitude, Haley | | ---|---|--- * A personal note from Haley 👋 I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love. But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican. I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win. If you're with me, will you chip in today? Paid for by Haley Stevens for Senate. | | | (C) 2026 Haley for MI 33717 Woodward Ave #539, Birmingham, MI 48009 ? ?

We wanted to make sure you saw this important request from James.
We’re not asking millions of people. We are asking you — because that’s how much your support matters to our movement.
The truth is things have slowed down now. Like James said, this won’t be won or lost in a day. And with early voting happening, every day is Election Day. That means every day we need to leave it all on the field to maintain our momentum and win on March 3.
**[So please, if you can help us put gas in the tank for the final stretch, make a contribution today. James needs all of us to have his back.](https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q1.AKJ3HX&refcode=em260221-1-ak&t=1&akid=461%2E1347274%2Ec0kezu)**

_James’ original message:_

Hey Peter, I’m not sending this email out to millions of people. It’s only going to a smaller number of folks like you who haven’t made a contribution to our U.S. Senate campaign yet.
You’ve likely heard that Trump’s FCC intimidated CBS corporate executives into censoring my interview with Stephen Colbert.
Donald Trump and his billionaire friends are worried that our movement is going to take back Texas.
The truth is it will require significant resources. We see clear as day what we will have to overcome.
We’ve had a big day, and we’re close to hitting a goal that I think would stun the political world. No, this race cannot be won in a single day, but if we pull this off, we can send a powerful message that the momentum — and more importantly, the people — are on our side.
**[If you believe in our movement, please consider making a contribution tonight. Again, I’m not sending this to millions of people. So if you’re able to pitch in right now, it will have an outsized impact.](https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q1.AKJ3HX&refcode=em260221-1-ak&t=2&akid=461%2E1347274%2Ec0kezu)**

James

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125861665/603141777/-306725926?refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.02.21_peltola-split_B1_F1_S1_C1_30do30dc60dd_N-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTkvMS83MjcyMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmYjA0OTdhZC01MDBmLWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2E1NzU5M2YiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=XSC1F00Rm_N7z-ZoLTqIsQs4uvf619X3PVg7i4inrBA=) When I was growing up, salmon fishing in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.

I still love to be outside. It reminds me of being a kid.

But the abundance I remember doesn’t exist anymore. Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.

Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.

So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families.

I’m tired of politicians in DC doing nothing to stop it. All while they profit off that very same system.

That’s why I’m running to fight for Alaska’s future. Systemic change is the only way to fill our homes with abundance again.

But it won’t be a smooth course to the finish line. We’re racing against corporate donors and dark money groups who are going to spend big because they don’t want the rigged system to change. They’re the only ones this broken system is working for!

_So here’s where the lessons I learned from dog mushing come in:_

**As long as we’re all pulling in the same direction, we can win this.**

It’s all about the team, and I know we have an amazing grassroots movement that can take this on. Thousands of people have already pitched in to help us win this seat because they want to unrig the system in DC.

Now, I’m hoping that today’s the day you can join them, because it all adds up when we chip in together.

So I’m asking:

[**_Split a donation of $10, or whatever you can, between my campaign and Kirsten Gillibrand to help us build on our grassroots momentum. Getting my salsa business off the ground was not an easy task, friend. I would drop my child off at school and immediately rush back home to work on my recipes.

Once I finally perfected my salsa recipe — roasted red chile, garlic, onion, tomatoes, oregano, and vinegar — it was time to start selling. From overseeing the work done in the commercial kitchen, to boxing up the salsa jars, to delivering them to stores in Los Lunas, Belen, Bernalillo, and more — I was a part of every step, making sure my small, but mighty, business would thrive.

There were long days and even longer nights, but it was worth it — knowing I was supporting my child, contributing to our local economy, and bringing our Pueblo culture into grocery stores across the state. I started this business so I could be more present for my child while still making ends meet, and it was the best way I knew to build a future for our family.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/4677?refcode=jtk274-fr-nat-nd&t=2&akid=7683%2E400544%2EvJSA0P)
While I no longer run my salsa business, I still cook every single day. The lessons I learned building that business are a lasting part of who I am. Small businesses are the backbone of New Mexico’s entrepreneurial spirit and economy, friend. As an entrepreneur myself, I know what it takes to start from scratch, and I’ll always stand up for small businesses and creative minds across our state.

I know that New Mexico can be a leader in so many things: advanced manufacturing, tech, film, clean energy, and so much more — but it starts with making sure people have the tools they need to make a business idea a reality.
**_[Please, will you rush $5 right now to help me win in New Mexico and take our state into the future?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/4677?refcode=jtk274-fr-nat-nd&t=3&akid=7683%2E400544%2EvJSA0P)_**

clean_body: | | | Peter, For weeks, Congress has been debating over whether to dump more tax dollars into the Department of Homeland Security — which means more money for ICE, and more warrantless arrests, home invasions, and fear in our communities. Last week, thanks to pressure from people like you across the country, Senate Democrats stood their ground. They voted against funding DHS through September, blocking both the long-term bill and a short, two-week extension. The only Democrat to break ranks and side with Republicans? Pennsylvania Senator John Fetterman. Now the real question: will Democrats hold that line in the next vote? That’s exactly what we’re organizing to ensure. Let’s be crystal clear: we don’t want another dimegoing to ICE. We want our tax dollars to fund homes, jobs, and care — not raids, violence, and fear. That means funding for: Homes we can afford. Meaningful jobs to support ourselves and our families. Childcare when and where we need it. Healthcare we can actually rely on. In solidarity, Team WFP Thoughts? Feedback? We want to hear it. Reply directly to this email and let us know. This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. If you received this email as a forward and want to get the latest updates from the Working Families Party directly, The Working Families Party is the party of the multiracial working class, fighting for a nation that cares for all of us. body:
The governor has officially signed off on the new congressional maps. Now, we need you.
# [](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/629?refcode=em20260221-216&t=1&akid=216%2E12592%2E05c1_X)
Breaking news: **Governor Abigail Spanberger has signed off on the new congressional maps to be used in the midterms.**
[](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260221_2.2L51Vp&amount=3&refcode=20260221-216&t=2&akid=216%2E12592%2E05c1_X)
That means the new lines are _set_.
The path to flipping four of Virginia’s Republican-held U.S. House seats is _real_.
With these maps, we could have an election that gives voters fair representation in Congress to level the playing field after Republican legislatures around the country rigged their own maps at Trump’s request.
Virginia’s response is official. **Now, we need your help to make it happen.**
**[Urgently, donate $10 or more today to help us make sure voters know what’s at stake this April. We don’t have much time to get the word out about voting YES for fair elections, so if you’ve been waiting to chip in, now is the time.](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260221_2.2L51Vp&refcode=20260221-216&t=3&akid=216%2E12592%2E05c1_X)**

Hi friends. Warning — if you don’t want to be enraged to the point of seeing red, you might want to delete this email right now.
Still reading? Here’s a headline for you:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25]
This pastor — who we’ve had the displeasure of discussing before, last time Pete Hegseth lifted up his twisted views — is our Defense Secretary’s (sorry, War Secretary’s) personal spiritual leader.
On top of his disturbing and shameful views on slavery — he actually describes himself as a “paleo-confederate” — this guy also thinks we should criminalize homosexuality, and he has a whole lot to say about women and our role in society .
Wives should submit to their husbands. The 19th Amendment should be repealed because granting women the right to vote was a “bad idea.”
To be extremely clear: My role in society isn’t to submit to a man. It’s to be a Member of Congress.
And a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee and Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Africa. And a member of the House Armed Services Committee. And to serve as the Parliamentarian in the House Democratic Caucus, one of the youngest members of Democratic House leadership.
Get the picture, pastor?
Anyway — what does all this have to do with...everything else? Well for starters, Pete Hegseth invited this pastor to preach at the Pentagon this week, where he delivered a sermon (paid for by our tax dollars!) to military personnel. It’s offensive to our troops, to people of color, to women, and to American taxpayers.
None of us can be shocked anymore by this administration, and certainly not by Pete Hegseth. He’s platformed some of the most vile views out there, and he’s going to keep doing it as long as he can.
But while we can’t be shocked, we CAN remain outraged — and channel that anger into getting these racist, sexist, homophobic, egotistical losers out of power so they stop infecting our country with their rot and putting us on the fast-track to white nationalism and authoritarianism.
That’s my mission this year, and I know we can do it.
Republicans currently have a one-seat margin of error in their majority, and we’ve got so many incredible Democrats on the ballot this year.
But it won’t happen on its own, without our sincere effort.
So please — join my work today by contributing any amount, and let’s get ready to knock it out of the park in November. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25]

NC Newsline: Amid protests, NC elections board rejects campus voting sites and Sunday voting in several counties [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=022126_1&amount=25]
We're facing the repercussions of the partisan election takeover laws that went into effect at the end of 2024, Team.
To refresh your memory: After the 2024 elections and the defeat of a MAGA candidate for governor, opponents of voting rights in North Carolina jammed through a bill that took the power of the governor to appoint people to election boards and handed that to the state auditor . It's worth noting that the state auditor is the only statewide elected Republican, with Democrats winning the 2024 races for governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general, and secretary of state.
Now, among massive protests from young voters, the MAGA-fied North Carolina State Elections Board recently shot down proposals to continue having early voting sites at several universities around the state . These weren't new sites either; these were places where North Carolina had provided early voting locations for a decade or more.
This is voter suppression, plain and simple, by making it harder for eligible, registered voters to vote in-person by taking away their polling place. It's another demonstration of how opponents of voting rights in North Carolina are more focused on expanding and cementing their own power than they are in serving the people and having fair elections.
We have to fight these suppressive actions in North Carolina and any other state where opponents of voting rights try to replicate this. These new, highly partisan State Election Board members wouldn't even look the protestors in the eye or engage with their proposals. After the vote, Chairman Francis De Luca threatened to call the cops on students if they didn’t leave.
Need to better understand how this impacts young voters? Western Carolina University in Jackson County, for example, has had a polling place on campus since 2016 that’s been used in five general elections and four primaries, according to a document prepared for the board. The state board voted 3-2 to get rid of it.
Closing the campus voting site would not save money, but “ would create barriers to voting for young, rural residents ,” Jackson County Board member Betsy Swift told the state board. 64% of students don’t have vehicles to drive to the polling place, she said.
Without the on-campus site, the closest polling place for students will be a recreation center nearly two miles away. Students without transportation will have to walk along a four-lane highway and through a meadow to get there.
Voter suppression isn't just black and white photos of eligible voters being turned away from polling places. Voter suppression is making it harder for eligible voters to take part in our elections through onerous ID requirements, closing polling places, taking away voting locations, or ending mail-in voting. Every time someone makes it harder to cast your ballot, voters are suppressed.
It's not going to end until we stop them.

name: Squad Victory HQ
subject: Honoring Black History
body:
[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/18910?refcode=em20260221-1960-foote&t=1001&akid=1960%2E342411%2EHYFWBG ]Squad Victory Fund

Peter,

Black History Month is a celebration, a remembrance, and a call to action.

It’s a time to honor the Black organizers, educators, artists, workers,
elders, and young leaders whose courage and brilliance have shaped this
country at every turn. Their leadership doesn’t just live in history
books. It guides our movement today.

Because Black history is American history.

But as we celebrate and uplift Black excellence, we cannot ignore the fact
that this administration and its allies are trying to systematically
whitewash our history, rewrite Black stories and censor the truth. They
use words like “DEI,” “wokeness,” “CRT,” and “BLM.” But what they mean is
Black. We won’t let their thinly veiled attempts at anti-Blackness dull
our resolve to loudly and joyfully celebrate Black history.

While some try to erase the resilience, resistance, and achievements of
the Black community, we refuse to let these stories, these struggles, or
these voices be silenced.

So this Black History Month, we celebrate Black lives, Black families, and
Black futures. We celebrate the victories won. We acknowledge the work
still ahead. And we stand firm in our commitment to building a future that
is more equitable, more inclusive, and more just.

In solidarity,

Squad Victory HQ

subject: I couldn’t wait until Monday

body:
# [](https://act.chrisforjustice.com/go/18?refcode=em20260221-1144&t=1&akid=1148%2E294397%2EqO1yBc)
Can I be honest?
I told myself I’d wait until Monday to check our fundraising numbers.
I couldn’t.
I logged in this morning to see how we’re pacing, and during the holiday weekend, we took a bit of a dip. Things haven’t picked up since.
I get it. People are spending time with family instead of checking their email.
But here’s the thing:
We’re less than two months out from the April election. Our extreme opponent is already on the air. And keeping our campaign firing on all cylinders takes real resources.
If we slow down, even for a few days, it adds up fast.
**You’re on Judge Chris Taylor’s supporter list for a reason.** Maybe this is your first week with us. Maybe you’ve been here for months.
Either way, this is one of those moments where stepping up _really_ matters.
[**If you’re able, will you chip in today to help us pick up the pace and keep building toward April? Any amount will help us get out of this fundraising slump.**](https://act.chrisforjustice.com/go/31?c0=em_ms_jct_20260221_1_ak.FSERxt&amount=10&refcode=em20260221-1144&t=3&akid=1148%2E294397%2EqO1yBc)

| | **At the end of last year, I wrapped up my 1138th town hall.** Every year I serve in the Senate, I pledge to hold open-to-all town meetings in each of Oregon's 36 counties. So far in 2026, I've hosted 11 town meetings. These town halls are for you: listening to the concerns of Oregonians and answering your questions. In 2025, I heard many shared concerns from Oregonians throughout the year:
* People worry about soaring health care costs. Too many Oregon families are being forced to make tough choices between covering the cost of prescriptions or paying for rent and groceries.
* People want the truth about the Epstein files. Why did the Trump administration withhold the files for so long, and why do they continue to hide the full story?
* Communities are fearful of masked and unidentified ICE agents snatching people off the streets with no due process.
* Oregonians want accountability for Trump and his cronies trampling over the Constitution.

Donald Trump has been dangerously emboldened by a Republican majority in Congress that is running scared from its own constituency. Republicans have pretty much stopped hosting any public town halls for fear of facing tough questions from their districts about enabling Trump's lawlessness. But I believe that if you aren't hearing directly from the people you represent, you can't do your job. Town halls are the most important part of my career in public service. As long as I have the honor to represent Oregon in the Senate, I will always give Oregonians a platform to hold their elected officials accountable. The will of the people is our best weapon right now, and we must harness it at every level in every fight ahead. And similarly, our collective people-power helped block millions of dollars for ICE and CBP in Congress’s continuing resolution. Thank you for making the effort, making a call to Congress and showing up for our communities! **Moments like these are reminders of what our people-power can accomplish. Thank you for making the effort, making a call to Congress and showing up for our communities! Moments like these are reminders of what our people-power can accomplish. But this fight isn’t over yet. body:
This gives us hope.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260221-1&t=1&akid=3173%2E587540%2Eg-OB7v)
Peter,
This is giving us hope.
In the November election in Virginia, **turnout among voters under 30 increased by more than 50% compared to 2021.**
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260221_1_virginia.KsUhpj&refcode=em20260221-3173&amount=5&t=2&akid=3173%2E587540%2Eg-OB7v)
And the results were huge. Democrats in Virginia won the governorship, the lieutenant governorship, held and expanded their majority in the House of Delegates, and won the Attorney General race. That means Democrats now have the power to shape what happens next, from redistricting decisions to abortion rights protections for Virginians.
**Young people helped make this happen, Peter.**
They showed up, they organized, _and_ they proved that when young voters turn out, we can get the results we’ve been fighting for.
Young people aren’t just any other demographic in our politics anymore. **This year, Gen Z and Millennials will make up roughly _half_ of eligible voters in the country.** They are living with the highest costs, the most uncertainty, and a political system that too often does _not_ deliver. And still, they are showing up. But to ensure we keep up the momentum long term and don't have young people turn right again like they did in 2024, we have to show them how we are not the same party as we were in 2024 — we have fresh faces and new ideas.
Right now, some states are already in early voting mode, and there is a real chance to build power and vote for people who will actually get the job done. So if you can, **[will you pitch in $5 to help us reach more voters and support more young progressive candidates?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260221_1_virginia.KsUhpj&refcode=em20260221-3173&amount=5&t=3&akid=3173%2E587540%2Eg-OB7v)**

The Corporation for Public Broadcasting — which helped fund NPR, PBS and many local radio and TV stations – voted to dissolve the private, nonprofit corporation after 58 years of service.

For more than half a century, it ensured that all Americans — regardless of their zip code, income, or background — had access to trusted news, educational programming.

Peter, President Trump and Republicans started this nationwide redistricting crisis with mid-decade gerrymanders in Texas, North Carolina, and Missouri. And they’re not subtle about their plans to further manipulate the map in Florida. **The good news is that Virginia is fighting back for a level playing field.** While Republicans continue to bypass the people to force through egregious mid-decade gerrymanders, Virginia lawmakers are letting the voters decide whether the state should redraw its map to counter GOP power grabs. Look, no one wants to be in the middle of a redistricting crisis. But now that Republicans have led us down this path, we’re certainly not going to helplessly stand by while they rig the midterms in their favor. [**The NDRC is leading the fight across the country to defend our democracy from Republican attacks — and we need your help. Can you chip in today?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125868510/603162548/-2069046819?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_VirginiaUpdate_email_20260221-NDRC-Tier1-VirginiaUpdate_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260221-NDRC-Tier1-VirginiaUpdate_&utm_campaign=VirginiaUpdate&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjc1NzllMGFlLTY5MGYtZjExMS1hNjlhLTAwMGQzYTU3NTkzZiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=0Uz-I-tN15iQt0yFtJ42d5uP2leBhBuzZyev-rx8rXk=) Ultimately, we must do everything we can to end partisan gerrymandering and ensure that redistricting is an independent process to ensure our democracy is truly representative of the people. Friend, My grandparents escaped the Nakba in 1948, and I'm a proud Palestinian American. But that isn't the reason why I use my voice to speak out against the genocide in Gaza or why I'm fighting so hard to stop our country from arming Netanyahu's government. **It's because I have a conscience.**
---
| [ ](https://ka4il.us/l/Uqc7Dv8WQKhJ)
---
Despite a lack of news coverage, the situation in Gaza is still dire, and the occupation of Palestinian land through settlements, which is illegal under international law, is still ongoing. And even though he recently met with President Trump, the International Criminal Court **_still_** has a warrant out for Benjamin Netanyahu's arrest. Friend, we need to stand united against the atrocities being committed in Gaza and call it what it is—a genocide. **And out of the 3 frontrunners in this race, I'm the only one to do that.** **I'm also the only one who opposes anti-BDS legislation as a free speech issue.** **And I'm the only one who hasn't met with or ever wanted to meet with AIPAC.** Friend, emails like this are exactly why groups like AIPAC are spending millions against me and uplifting my opponents. And it's why your support is so important. [**Will you please donate $5, $15, our average contribution amount of $32, or even $1 to help us counter their spending in our race?**](https://ka4il.us/l/djpMT2lnPIVn)
---
[ DONATE TODAY ](https://ka4il.us/l/vTL9seqERjYG)
---

**_Donald Trump is planning on attacking payment processor ActBlue in another attempt by his administration to push the limits of his power._**
The detainment of Mahmoud Kahlil, the deportation of Kilmar Abrego Garcia, and the outright denial to follow a ruling made by the Supreme Court are all blatant oversteps that attack our right to free speech and due process and challenge the rule of law.
Friend, I've spent years watching Fox News and listening to their rhetoric get more and more extreme, and Donald Trump is doing exactly what they want.
**_Fascism is, and has always been, their end goal._**
Their vision is one of a militarized country where only certain people—a few dozen rich men—have a seat at the table, and dissidents like me are silenced.
Trump and Elon know that progressive movements like ours are in the way because I've made it abundantly clear that strongly worded letters, wearing matching outfits while holding up signs, and meaningless acts of symbolism **aren't my thing.**
As a member of Congress, I'm going to be unwavering in my fight for our communities.
I will not vote for authoritarian bills in the name of "compromise," I will not abandon or demonize vulnerable groups to cater to the right, and I will not change my stances for fear of retaliation.
And Friend, that's what this action on ActBlue is: retaliation. Campaigns like ours rely on small dollars from people like you to support us, and ActBlue is integral to making that work.
[**If you can before you go, can you chip in (through ActBlue) to help us continue to fund mutual aid efforts and bring our unwavering commitment to the people of our district to Congress?**](https://ka4il.us/l/z505piPjdg35)
---

Our email sending software likes it when we have "clicks", but we don't always ask you to click a donation link. **[If you want to take 5 seconds helping us (for free), please click this link to our website after reading every email to help increase our "clickers".](https://ka4il.us/l/JlLwZX0WNrVv) **

We understand that email can be overwhelming. If you only want to receive the most important emails, click [here](https://ka4il.us/fewer-emails?email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&t=XKjqjH9v3JKQ). If you're really just sick of every email, click [here](https://ka4il.us/l/kahvkuFixZ6i) and you'll be unsubscribed!
---
| **_Democratic leaders are abandoning us._** Our District deserves a fighter in Congress — someone who shows her constituents every day that she is doing everything possible to stop the authoritarian takeover of the United States. Kat has fought fascists before as a citizen, union rep, and independent journalist. Now, she's going to do the same in Congress. **Let's win this together.** **[Chip in!](https://ka4il.us/l/dnMhjZ64berm)**

Fellow Patriot,
The war on President Trump started the instant he stepped off that golden escalator in 2015 and promised to put America First.
**The Democrat Machine, their media pawns, and entrenched Deep State bureaucrats declared total war with no rules and no mercy.**
They hit him with the **Russia witch hunt** that dragged on for years, costing hundreds of millions and tearing the country apart.
When that collapsed, they pivoted straight to the **impeachment effort** – a manufactured crisis built on lies, designed to nullify your vote and remove a duly elected President.
And even after they lost, they didn’t stop. They kept coming – _**more investigations, lawfare traps, endless smears, corrupt indictments and convictions.**_
Through all this and worse, President Trump survived, persevered and prevailed – winning a stunning comeback for a second term to help save this country we love so dearly.
**_But the radicals never quit. They’re still burning with rage._**
**And now, Alexander Vindman – the man who helped to orchestrate the entire failed impeachment effort and nearly killed MAGA – is back. And he's out for cold, hard revenge.**

Derek,
I wanted you to hear it from me directly:
**_I’m boycotting Trump’s State of the Union on Tuesday._**
And I wanted you to know exactly why.
This isn’t a decision I made lightly. I’ve never skipped a State of the Union address before, under Democratic or Republican presidents. No matter what they did.
But Donald Trump is destroying the very fabric of this country and turning it into something that is not a democracy.
This is something I cannot and will not abide.
He’s spent the first year of this term making lives worse for Americans. Slashing health care, sending masked ICE agents to murder our neighbors, and passing tax cuts for the rich, all while he corruptly cashes in for himself.
He violates the law, ignores court orders, tries to silence his opposition, and shows nothing but contempt for our Constitution.
This is intolerable, and I will not act as if this SOTU is like any other. Because the State of Our Union is in desperate trouble. And I will not give Donald Trump the attention he craves, or stand and applaud his many lies to the American people.
Instead, I will be in front of the Capitol, speaking to the public, along with many of my Senate colleagues. We will make a very different kind of address at the People’s State of the Union this Tuesday at 8 pm Eastern.
**_We cannot treat this State of the Union like business as usual. Because it isn’t._**
More from me soon,
Adam

name: Katie Porter
subject: Fuck Trump
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Katie Porter for Governor 2026
body:
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=40884%2E3422442%2EotHIvd)
_**Katie Porter just spoke at the California Democratic Party Convention, please take a moment to read her remarks below and[then donate to her campaign for governor.](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20260221_2_ak.KX_T4M&refcode=em20260221-40884&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=40884%2E3422442%2EotHIvd)**_
I’m Katie Porter. Some of you know me as the whiteboard lady who held CEOs and billionaires accountable in Congress.
So today, I wanna start with one simple, powerful message we all agree on.
Say it with me. Ready, 1 ... 2 ... 3...
_**Fuck Trump.**_
Yeah, that’s right, Fuck Trump. Together, we’re going to kick Trump’s ass in November and stop him in his tracks.
I’ll stand up to Trump and his cronies again and again, just as I did in Congress—with or without my whiteboard. But this election for Governor is about far more than defeating Trump.
We _**KNOW**_ what Trump is willing to do and how far he’s willing to go—he’s willing to kill people in the streets, to rip health care away, to ruthlessly attack our democracy.
But this governor’s race asks US—what are WE willing to do? What is CALIFORNIA willing to do for our democracy?
Who we elect as our next Governor is the biggest, most powerful statement we can make in 2026 about who Democrats are, in California, and nationally. About what we stand for, and about what we will do.
Let’s elect a bold leader who WILL DO big things—the things we have long fought for. When I’m your governor, I will deliver:
* Single payer health care,
* Less expensive housing,
* Free child care for all,
* Zero tuition charges at our UCs and CSUs,
* And, thousands of dollars back in families pockets, by eliminating California income tax for those earning less than $100,000.

Those are real affordability solutions!
For decades, we have fought for these ideas. We’ve organized. We’ve voted. We’ve pushed this party to be better.
I am running for Governor because I am WILLING and READY to get those things done!
But you know who is standing in our way? Billionaires and huge corporations that have far too much power in our country—and too much influence in Sacramento. I’ll take them DOWN and LIFT UP the working people of this state.
Look, I understand, there’s a lot that makes me unique in this race—and some of that scares people. I’m the single mom of three kids, I push a grocery cart, fill my minivan with gas, and pay the bills. I understand what it’s like to watch expenses like utilities and insurance go up and dollars not stretch far enough, because I’ve experienced that too.
We’ve never had a governor like that in California. Heck, we’ve never had a governor in heels! And I think it’s about damn time.
My differences will make me a better Governor, better able to address the challenges Californians face.
California Democrats, our country is counting on us to lead the way—to send a message about our democracy—by rejecting billionaires and corporate-backed candidates—and picking as governor, the ONLY candidate who has NEVER taken a dime of corporate PAC money.
In this election, there is a very real possibility that Republicans could sneak two candidates into the runoff. We CANNOT let that happen.
But let’s aim higher than stopping them. Let’s seize the opportunity to elect someone who is WILLING to get big things done and READY to live up to our progressive ideals.
My campaign IS our Democratic values, powered by small donations from 70,000 people just like you. And how you campaign is how you serve. I humbly ask for your support, not to be Governor “Of” California, but to Govern FOR ALL Californians.
Thank you.
_And Fuck Trump._
Katie Porter is running for governor to stand up to Trump and lower costs for working families. We need your help to win.

Katie is running to be California’s next governor because California and our country need a leader who will stand up to Trump to lower costs, protect our rights, and combat climate change. **[Donate ›››](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kp4g-em-footer?refcode=em20260221-40884&amounts=&t=5&refcode2=40884_3422442_otHIvd&akid=40884%2E3422442%2EotHIvd)**

**by Jonathan Larsen**
Members of Congress return next week and there will be more pressure to make a deal to renew funding for the Department of Homeland (sic) Security (DHS). This will be magical pressure because only Democrats will feel it.
The question is, will they still be feeling pressure from the people?
On Wednesday, the DHS ordered agents to start imprisoning _refugees_ --who entered legally because "refugee"--even if they've already begun the application process for a green card. They will be held in cages for the entire duration of the application process to ensure they're not making the U.S. economy more productive or lowering the crime rate by being out there committing fewer crimes than Americans.
And they're going to be _vetted_.
Advocacy groups say we're talking about an estimated 100,000 people. Acting ICE Director **Todd Lyons** claims that the law now suddenly requires ICE to vet them all.
> This requires DHS to take the affirmative actions of locating, arresting, and taking the alien [sic] into custody
Lyons presumably wrote this after giving ChatGPT a prompt to be fascist _and_ politically incorrect. And of course _now_ affirmative action is okay.
And refugees aren't the only you're-shitting-me class of human Trump is caging.
Because if there's one thing we can be sure of about Trump and the ladies, it's that he does _not_ like it when they get pregnant. I mean, he's been burned before...

So, shockingly but not surprisingly, we're finding out in court about Trump officials abusing pregnant people and new mothers in federal custody.
Separated from infants who are still nursing. Pregnant women housed in cramped and shoddy ICE cages.
Legal filings reveal multiple miscarriages of justice and also the other kind.
Pres. **Joe Biden** implemented policies to limit detention of women who are pregnant or nursing. But ICE won't tell us whether they aborted that policy. Which is weird because I'm pretty sure they're asking us for money right now.
Migrant Insider's **Pablo Manriquez** reports that ICE is raiding dormitories at the Dilley, TX, family-friendly concentration camp. How come?
As **Allison Gill** explained, kids imprisoned there had written letters--not to be confused with diaries!--about their imprisonment. And ICE, apparently, was hunting for and confiscating the letters after hunting for and confiscating the kids.
Also, the Justice Department admitted Wednesday that it's violated immigration and detainee court orders at least 52 times. _Just_ in New Jersey, replacing The Sopranos as the state's number-one crime family.

### **Here 's how Americans are fighting back**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/52d3696d-60c7-477f-8664-3d5db4b20268?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Gov. **Wes Moore** (D-MD) on Tuesday signed a new state law that prohibits local agreements to help out federal immigration predators.
That's what Maine did last month. And New Mexico earlier this month. And New York is about to do.
Democrats who run cities are also de-ICE-ing their streets. According to the Washington Post, mayors in Boston, Chicago, Los Angeles, New York, Oakland and Seattle are restricting where and how ICE and CBP can operate there.
In some cities, **local police are monitoring the activities of these dangerous gangs**.
The Public Rights Project is helping dozens--plural--of cities draft local immigration laws **immune to federal legal challenges**.
Prosecutors in about a dozen cities and counties--including Austin, Dallas, Tucson, and Virginia's Arlington and Fairfax counties--are warning they'll _prosecute_ criminal gang members. Philadelphia District Attorney **Larry Krasner** , a Democrat, has reminded these rampaging gangs publicly that they can be prosecuted because their sexual predator president lacks the power to pardon them in states or cities.
Of course, judges have been on the front lines--metaphorically speaking--all along. And on Wednesday, one judge broke through to strike behind enemy lines.
In Minneapolis, federal Judge **Laura Provinzino** had ordered ICE to return an undocumented immigrant's documents--after ICE released him--because he's been pursuing legal status for years. ICE didn't do it.
**So Provinzino found Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Matthew Isihara in civil contempt and punished him with a fine of $500. EVERY DAY, until the documents are returned**.
Isihara, by the way, is a Defense Department JAG,1 on loan to the Justice Department, and told Provinzino that DHS has saddled him with 130 cases in just the past month. Dude, quit-yer whining and quit your job. I mean, ICE is hiring!

Sen. **Roger Wicker** (R-MS)--absolutely **not** pictured above--asked DHS Secretary **Kristi Noem** to keep her stinkin' concentration camps out of Mississippi. One camp, anyway.
Apparently Wicker thinks the local infrastructure and social services aren't sufficient to support a concentration camp with 8500 prisoners. Even _with_ the robust economy and rampant development inspired by the low, low taxes of Mississippi!
And apparently someone explained to Noem just how Mississippi, Mississippi actually is, so she agreed. But it's not just Republican politicians pushing back.
The New York Times spoke to a whole bunch of Trump supporters who never thought he'd ship scary people to warehouses in _their_ town. The administration is planning a new concentration camp in Surprise, AZ, and Trump's voters there aren't happy about it.
Local cheerleading gym owner **Stacy Bradley** is happy that Trump is hurting the right people, but she's upset that a new concentration camp will be next door to her gym. Surprise!
Councilman **Chris Judd** said DHS isn't telling the town jack about caging people not named Jack. He said, "Not having any information coming from the feds as to what we need to do or what's going to happen is very frustrating." Sure, but then it wouldn't be a Surprise.

When others give in, I don’t. I dig in. For our values, our rights, and our future. I don’t sit up next to MAGA puppets and nod along to their lies. I don’t amplify their falsehoods when it suits my needs. At the end of the day -- I make it clear exactly who and what I am fighting for. When our communities are under assault and extremists are stripping away freedoms we’ve spent generations fighting for, I don’t believe in going on TV to posture for a media circuit that thrives on false balance. I believe in organizing. I believe in showing up. I believe in fighting back. That’s what I’ve been doing alongside Texans who are living with the consequences of Republican extremism every single day. This race is about values, and it’s about backbone. It’s about whether we send someone to the Senate who stands for something, or someone who will say whatever plays well in the moment — even if it means legitimizing voices that work against everything Democrats believe in. Texas cannot afford a Senator who is more interested in validation than in standing up for working people, voting rights, affordability, and our democracy. I have never been afraid to call out the far right, and I’m not confused about what real leadership looks like. It doesn’t happen on panels or through soundbites. Peter, here’s where we stand before tonight’s pre-primary deadline:

**[If you’re with me, can you rush a $5 contribution to help us get there?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260221_2_deadline.I4YvGp&refcode=em20260221-624&amount=5&t=1&akid=624%2E299639%2EjhMl1B)**

Everywhere we look, we see the consequences of Greg Abbott’s leadership:
* Neighborhood schools are closing
* Health care costs are skyrocketing while Texas ranks near the bottom in access to affordable, quality care
* Property taxes are unaffordable and getting worse
* People are struggling to afford the basics

**That’s why I’m running for Governor, Peter. Because Texans deserve better.**
But I know this race won’t be easy. Our opponent has more than $100 million in his campaign account — and he’ll spend whatever it takes to try to bring us down. | | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

name: Tobias Read
subject: How to make sure your ballot is counted under the new rule >>
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260221em-processing-pet [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260221em-processing-pet]
I want to flag something important — and honestly, a little alarming.
A new U.S. Postal Service rule that went into effect on Christmas Eve quietly changed how postmarks are defined. That might sound technical, but stick with me — it has real consequences for everyday people, including whether your ballot counts and whether time-sensitive documents like tax returns are considered on time.
Here’s the change: A postmark used to generally reflect the day you dropped your mail off. Now, it officially reflects the day your mail is processed — which could be days later, depending on how far your local post office is from a regional processing center.
Why does that matter?
In states where mail-in ballots must be postmarked by Election Day, this change could mean the difference between your vote being counted or rejected — even if you did everything right.
As the Postal Service consolidates processing facilities, many post offices are now 50 to 150 miles away from where mail is actually postmarked. That distance creates delays that voters can’t control.
This isn’t just about elections. It affects tax filings, legal documents, and any deadline-driven mail that relies on a postmark.
There are ways to protect yourself:
* Bring time-sensitive mail to a staffed post office counter and request a free manual postmark
* Mail important items earlier than you think you need to
* For taxes, confirm whether private carriers are allowed for your filing
* Always check your state and local election rules
I’m sharing this because democracy doesn’t fail all at once — it erodes quietly, through technical changes most people never hear about until it’s too late.
I’m fighting to make sure voters are protected, informed, and never silenced by bureaucracy. If you believe people shouldn’t lose their vote to a processing delay, please add your name to my petition to say you believe voters have the right to be heard.
